title: 《空战奇兵8 希孚之翼》今日上市！
text:
万代南梦宫娱乐宣布，广受好评的《空战奇兵》系列时隔七年的首部正统续作，PlayStation®5／Xbox Series X|S／STEAM®版《空战奇兵8希孚之翼》已于今（2）日于全球正式上市。同步公开上市宣传视频。
前往查看《空战奇兵8希孚之翼》上市宣传视频
由Bandai Namco Aces Inc.开发的《空战奇兵8希孚之翼》利用Unreal® Engine 5与独家技术打造出极度逼真的空中激战体验，带领玩家翱翔天际，并将本飞行射击游戏系列推向新高度。本作亦提供系列迄今为止规模最大的多人游戏体验，来自世界各地的飞行员可透过跨平台功能，共同游玩各种刺激的在线模式。
《空战奇兵8希孚之翼》延续系列所缔造的传奇，将飞行射击游戏的画面表现与街机风格的空战动作推向全新高度。本作藉由次世代主机性能及万代南梦宫自主研发的独家技术，呈现出极具沉浸感的飞行体验。除了收录多种存在于现实世界中的战斗机，更透过广阔逼真的云层以及细致渲染的地形与环境，展现出令人惊叹的视觉效果。此外，天气也会大大影响游玩过程，玩家必须应对这些具有挑战性的状况。
第一人称视角且宛如电影的剧情演出也进一步增强了故事的沉浸感，玩家将能更身临其境地体验战斗场面，并深入了解身处冲突核心的飞行员们。
在故事中，玩家将置身于一个战火纷飞的世界。这个世界虽源于本系列的虚构宇宙，但抉择的分量、指挥的压力以及在战斗中结下的情谊，却令人感到无比真实。
中尤联邦（FCU）已被占领，军事力量溃散，民众艰难求生。玩家将化身为被冠以首都希孚之名、呼号为＂希孚之翼＂的王牌飞行员，并与Joker队成员巴克斯塔、塔莎和科斯达并肩作战，对抗入侵的索托亚共和国并收复家园。
随着战况加剧，玩家不仅要面对压倒性的敌方兵力及强大的对手飞行员，还将面临种种左右FCU命运的抉择。
《空战奇兵8希孚之翼》包含系列史上最大规模的在线多人游玩模式，玩家可自订佣兵飞行员，并进入全新的虚拟大厅──也就是支持至多100名来自世界各地及不同平台的玩家同时连线的空军基地。在线战斗包含Co-Op Assault与Co-Op Warfare模式，以及限时紧急任务和PvP活动。在线模式拥有独立的进度、报酬、训练、街机及点唱机等内容，飞行员们将能以崭新的方式结伴翱翔于天际。
《空战奇兵8希孚之翼》提供的PREMIUM ACE PASS可使用于ACE COMBAT ONLINE。PREMIUM ACE PASS除了可单独购买之外，亦包含于数字豪华版的PREMIUM ACE PASS PLUS Voucher内，可在上市后用于解锁一季分量的内容。
玩家可使用PREMIUM ACE PASS立即解锁30等级，以获得前30等级的季度报酬。此外，在季度中还可获得机体涂装、虚拟化身服装以及可操作机体＂ADFX-02
Morgan -PIXY-＂作为额外报酬。

title: 前《妙鸭》核心团队创业，跨界做了一款AI乙女游戏
text:
前《妙鸭》核心团队创业，跨界做了一款AI乙女游戏
游戏新知君
2026-10-02 11:01 发布于 湖北 游戏新知官方账号
关注
题 图 |《星眠 》
作者 | 夜风
AI乙游《星眠》近日 （9月29日） 刚刚结束二测。
值得注意的是，《星眠》是最早拿到游戏版号的AI乙游，也有望成为最快上线的AI乙游之一。
《星眠》背后的团队 颇为 特殊：它由北京沐言智语研发，CEO 张月光是互联网行业资深的 明星产品人 。
张月光毕业于清华大学计算机系，一毕业便进入阿里巴巴。四年后，他加入字节跳动，出任时光相册产品负责人， 主导这款核心产品从 0 到 1 的打造 。 此后，他以创业者身份完成了一段独立操盘的历练，带着更完整的视野回归阿里 ，成为公司最年轻的产品总监 （M4/P9） 之一。在阿里期间，他主导打造的 AI 应用《妙鸭相机》现象级破圈， 成为行业级爆款 。
2023年，张月光从阿里离开，创业了沐言智语。有公开报道称，沐言智语成立后已先后完成四轮融资，总融资金额可能近3亿人民币，公司估值已过亿美元。
在《妙鸭相机》之后，核心团队又陆续做过一些AI产品，不过《星眠》还是他们第一次跨界做游戏。
整个女性向赛道对于「AI+乙游到底是什么样」想象了这么久，现在终于又能看到一份答卷了。
从二测版本来看，尽管加入了AI聊天、 日记、互动剧场等一系列  AI 功能，《星眠》在整体上还是 尊重了乙游成熟的 产品形态。
玩家可以输入文本来与星眠对话，随着等级和亲密度的提升，还能解锁换装、专注、日记等玩法。特别之处在于，玩家与星眠之间的互动、对星眠说过的事，都有可能出现在他的日记 （航行日志） 里面， 这也是《星眠》的另一个亮眼的AI玩法 。成为两人相处记忆的一部分，还挺有「活人感」的。 卡面叠花之后，也可以解锁角色特定身份剧情下的AI聊天和剧场功能。
玩家的实际体验
除了AI互动功能之外，游戏以偏放置的模拟经营为主要玩法，剧情则仍然以AVG形式呈现。剧情关卡之间也零星插入了战斗关卡作为数值验证，战斗玩法是比较基础的卡牌数值对对碰，可以直接放置自动进行，完全没有操作门槛。
模拟经营玩法
相比数值验证，游戏在AVG的演出效果方面下了更多功夫，一个很大的特色是把AI能力结合进了AVG玩法之中。在第一章剧情中，玩家被卷入了一个类似平行世界的地方，需要在一个直播系统的引导下完成任务，才能存活下来，返回自己的世界。剧情中会时不时插入弹幕互动环节，玩家可以混入观众之中自由输入弹幕并发送，紧接着就能获得其他观众的弹幕回复，相当有沉浸感。
发送弹幕
游戏新知和《星眠》制作人何泪泪深入聊了聊。何泪泪早在《妙鸭相机》时期就是张月光核心团队中的一员，也和张月光一样，还是第一次做游戏。但她对于《星眠》相当有信心。
何泪泪说： 「 我们不是在做一款AI聊天产品，我们是在用AI重构一种关系体验。游戏是我们选择的第一种载体，因为它能承载叙事、情感和互动。未来这种关系体验可以延展到更多形态，但游戏是我们认为最适合它生长的土壤。 」
她认为，《星眠》与其他AI乙游产品最大的不同是专注于「养关系」，这跳出了内容消费的框架，也是AI的加入对于传统乙游的最重要助力之一。
在她看来， AI 的能力可以使乙游带来全新的体验，反过来乙游也能使 AI 陪伴具有更成熟的商业模式 。而《星眠》目前已经完成了最基础的验证。
以下为访谈实录：
「人工筑IP，AI养关系」
游戏新知：《星眠》如何定义自己，它是一款加入了玩法的AI陪伴应用，还是一款带有AI交互功能的游戏？
何泪泪：确实现在AI陪伴产品立项了很多，但是真正把自己定位为AI 游戏 、特别是AI乙女游戏的其实没多少 。 一定要走游戏投入的，所以其实定位跟陪伴还不太一样。
我们当时其实想过到底要做陪伴还是游戏，这要看公司想怎么发展。 我们公司定下来的一个核心使命叫「创造AI朋友」，它的落脚点应该是和朋友的关系。
如果做AI陪伴应用，用户对IP的认知是需要持续发起话题、持续提供聊天动机来挖掘和探索，其实对用户的要求非常高，需要用户很强的创造力。我觉得这样对于关系 的发生，是一种阻力 。
而如果我们是一款游戏，游戏本身就有剧情和任务，有各种目标来推动用户继续挖掘，在这个过程中用户和男主有了共同经历，就可以更了解男主。用户完成了对IP的这样的整体认知，再去聊天和互动的时候，心理门槛其实是会大大降低的，对于我们的终极目标「让关系长出来」会更方便。
所以一方面我们决定要把《星眠》做到游戏内容的厚度，同时又把培养长期关系作为根本目的。
新知：具体是怎么用游戏的方法来做关系？
何泪泪：我们很早就想通了一个问题：要做游戏，就肯定要对游戏有敬畏之心，因为我毕竟不是游戏行业出身。我们团队有一个核心的准则： 「人工筑IP，AI养关系」 。
属于IP这条线的所有的美术文案等等，我们充分尊重传统游戏行业的成熟生产管线。在故事、美术、音乐、音效等等各方面，我们肯定要按照游戏的标准来卷，这些方面游戏行业已经是非常成熟的领域了。
新知：那么AI是如何加入游戏的？
何泪泪：我们认为AI给整个游戏提供了 定制感、沉浸感、陪伴感 ，这三个感其实指向的是不同的方向。
定制感就是千人千面，但是我要再强调一下，我们的千人千面不是指星眠，是指 用户和星眠的关系 。对于乙游来讲男主就是IP，如果调校两下男主人设就变了，就不能称之为IP了，IP就是要存在固定的内核的。所以定制的是用户和星眠的关系，而且是 深入 的关系。
沉浸感讲的是AI和AI功能，还有AI功能和传统游戏玩法之间的串联。我不希望每一个AI的功能是割裂的，聊天就是聊天。 《星眠》里玩家和星眠聊过的内容，可能会出现在他写的日记里，还可能会在触摸反馈的时候出现。 所以用户能感受到，他用无处不在的关注和爱意去包裹你，你的每一件小事在他心里都形成了非常深刻的烙印，你做任何一件事情都能感受到他好在乎你。这是AI功能之间串联的作用。
来自玩家的分享，日记里不仅有事无巨细的记录，还有星眠自己的小感想和小心思
更进一步就是AI功能和游戏玩法之间的串联， 我们内部有一些探索，且未来公测还会有更多尝试 。我认为这个才是AI游戏未来比较重要的一个部分。现在AI产生的context （上下文） ，和用户在游戏里留下的行为内容 不太能串起来，我觉得这很难让用户感知到AI功能带来的体验 。
未来应该AI功能和AI功能之间要串联，AI功能和游戏玩法之间也要串联。玩家对 AI做一件事情，对游戏的数值主循环应该产生影响，因为游戏的主推动力应该是目标导向，让玩家更想玩。
另外游戏里的一些行为，也应该要反向作用于AI。举个例子，今天你 （玩家） 去模拟经营玩法经营旅馆，接待一个客人的时间比较长，那么之后星眠是不是可以在日记里写她怎么跟客人说那么长时间话，有点吃醋。这种沉浸感才是 更真实 的，context和用户行为要循环在一起。
然后陪伴感我要特别强调一下， 陪伴感还原的是异性之间关系建立的从0到1的过程 。异性关系建立上头越快，下头就一定是越快的，最开始往往是因为具有异性特质的一些标签，比如男生很帅，女生很漂亮，但是关系如果想长久绝对不是靠这个，而是靠没有明显异性特质的标签，比如说善良、勇敢。所以我们游戏的功能设计和模型训练中会特别注意释放节奏，让用户真的能还原相识、相知、相许的整个过程。
新知：游戏里具体是如何引导玩家渐渐了解男主、建立关系的呢？
何泪泪：其实就是润物细无声了。比如剧情里，现在二测版本是 快穿 ，一开始玩家要去解救星眠、了解整个世界观，这些任务本身其实就是找寻价值意义的过程。其实一测的时候还不是这样，一测是温暖治愈的过程，要和星眠一起去拯救别人的梦境。但是我们觉得主线更多地应该符合市场喜好，所以就比较倾向于 快穿，快穿是比较容易发挥剧情的多样性，也能让玩家对和男主的约会陪伴场景持续产生新鲜感 。
内容方面一些玩法和功能也会慢慢去释放，比如一开始只能聊天，亲密度上涨之后，同一个问题星眠的回答可能是不一样的，最开始可能还克制一下，保持一下关系，慢慢就开始占有欲、开始腹黑了。一些AI功能也不是一开始就有，比如日记不会一开始就让你看，因为关系没到那份上，得慢慢来。还有专注功能，其实是星眠自己的一些爱好，包括画画和做饭，是因为本来他就会干他喜欢干的事情，只是因为爱你才会和你一起做。
玩家对专注功能的感想
新知：和同类型产品相比，《星眠》的核心优势是什么？
何泪泪：核心优势是我们想清楚了要做游戏这件事，所以我们在招人的时候还蛮明确的，就是IP打造 一定要是专业的女性向团队 ，应聘者一定要做过而且非常了解女性向游戏，了解用户和管线。
AI这一块，我们会一直坚持应用和模型一体、内容和技术一体，我们会 自训和自建模型 。我们整个算法团队背景是清华的，CEO也是清华的，团队中60%以上都是硕博，之前我们也做过2023年爆款的AI产品《妙鸭相机》，这些都是团队在AI上的沉淀。
我觉得只有这两部分人真正地结合好，我们这个团队才有可能把这个IP做深，也让AI真正实现定制感、沉浸感、陪伴感。我觉得这些都是我们的优势。
新知：和传统的乙游相比，AI的介入给游戏带来了怎样的影响？
何泪泪：刚刚大概也聊到核心是关于关系。我觉得大多数乙游本身还是内容消费 。 但是我觉得AI的加入真的是把内容消费变成关系入口。
可以试想一下，你 （玩家） 为什么会跟他聊天？你会分享你的一些所思所想、你看到的体验到的东西，时间长了之后，你分享的这些东西我们叫context，实际上我说得夸张点就代表了你的人格和灵魂。现实中就是这样，你交付这些东西给一个人建立信任的过程，你们就会越来越互相了解，然后互相磨合得越来越好，这个关系才是支撑这件事的核心。也许有一天关系会平淡一些，但是现实中的关系也是这样，所谓七年之痒往往是因为两个人进入到了一个固定模式，没有新鲜感了，但是没有新鲜感了不代表关系就要终止。
所以游戏里面，我们的活动也好，卡面也好，未来的故事，还有各种AI功能， 它们起到的作用是给你 （玩家） 提供场景 。你们俩已经建成关系了，这个关系是需要在场景里去发酵的，所以我 （游戏） 让你们一起做更多的事，一起经历更多的体验。但陪在你身边的还是这个人，这件事非常重要。
所以我觉得AI的加入在关系这件事上会有非常杰出的优势。另一方面来讲，这也会成为一个护城河，因为用户要建立关系，得付出真心、付出信任，这件事情需要时间。而我们因为各方面设计很好的引导，让用户愿意放下戒备，这两个东西都会是护城河。
新知：除了聊天功能之外，AI有没有更进一步影响游戏的玩法形态？
何泪泪：我们在AI的设计上会有三个层次的考虑。第一个层次是 增强本身的AVG体验 ，就是结合内容文案的能力，去设计能增强体验的一些玩法。比如二测里体验到的弹幕还有问卷等等，它也不是无处不在的，其实是跟文案的直播体的故事结合了之后顺理成章出现的。这一类设计可以让传统的AVG表演的整个体验都不一样，用户会很沉浸。
序章开头的问卷互动
第二个层次是 现有玩法的一些AI设计 ，会分为固定功能和一些活动玩法。用户在使用一些功能玩法的时候，能感受到定制感。举个例子，现在二测的时候有「焕新」功能，就是一键换装，这其实是第一个版本，和常见的乙游没什么区别，但是实际上我对这个功能的定位是 男女朋友讨论OOTD （Outfit of the Day，意为今日穿搭） 的地方 。以后你可以恶搞他，给他乱穿，他就可能会吐槽你；你在游戏里给他买了一件衣服，AI接收到了用户在游戏里留下的行为信号，他可能会说我今天要穿新衣服。
我们甚至还在尝试和 多模态模型 的结合 ，比如有没有可能开前置摄像头扫玩家身上的 衣服，星眠可能就说你今天穿成这样，那我要穿成什么样。这就是我说的场景还原。游戏的核心还是 深度 关系，所以我游戏的AVG也好，这些活动和功能也好，都是为了做场景，因为关系是需要场景才能沉淀的。
第三个层次是 参与主循环的一些AI设计 ，这是我们未来会加大投入的一个地方。就是刚刚讲到的让它更native一些，把AI玩法留下的context和用户行为之间串联起来，让它们互相影响，让整个管线运转起来。
新知：这些加入AVG玩法的AI互动功能，是怎么考虑加入的？
何泪泪：我觉得有两块，首先是从AI现有的能力出发，到底现在AI能做什么事，这些事怎么样能够放置在这个APP的体验中。第二个就是 一定要全方位地信任文案的创作 。因为比如弹幕这个功能，如果未来要出下一个场景，不适合弹幕的话，肯定会换一个形式，跟着场景变化去走。这个就不能剧透了，不过我们确实已经准备好了新的场景。
内部有一个「星眠设定手册」
新知：为什么《星眠》 现在 只有一位男主？会不会担心更难满足不同偏好的玩家？
何泪泪：其实现在也可以看到，星眠本身就会有不同的身份，这个之后还会越来越明显。我们其实是想在多男主 （的环境） 中去尝试一下，因为我们核心不是内容是关系。我们更强调玩家和男主建立的羁绊，能不能通过AI和agent管线的加入更长久，发展成一种长期关系。关系看的不是多少，是关系本身是什么样的，是否 深入 ，怎么发展，怎么给予用户足够的支撑和情绪价值。我们要围绕关系做更多的可能性。
左图的「相伴」是和星眠聊天的入口，右图卡牌页面的「依偎」是特定身份情境下的AI对话小剧场
新知：既然男主也预设了一定的性格特征，那么刚才提到的「定制感」要如何实现？玩家可以在什么程度上改变这份关系？
何泪泪：刚才我们已经形成一个共识，就是《星眠》的定制不是男主本身的改变，而是玩家和男主关系的改变。
另一方面从商业化上来说，我刚刚也说到IP要有足够稳定的人物内核。所以我们一开始就明确了一个设计逻辑，就是男主本身的人设性格不能变。其实模型在和用户的长期交互下越来越了解用户，真的可能会变得很不像自己，我们是花了大力气去控制的。 可以定制的是男主和玩家的关系，包括相处模式、情感氛围、共同的记忆和经历 ，这些是玩家可以改变的，也是可以让每个玩家的体验不一样的。
新知：在不同故事线中，星眠这个男主的身份和性格也会发生变化。游戏是怎么控制这个变化的程度的？
何泪泪：这个问题分为文案部分和AI训练部分。文案部分其实就是传统游戏的一套供货逻辑，文案团队要写大纲，什么时候出什么样的变化，各种节点和里程碑全部都要提前预设好，然后才能保证设定不要出问题。
其实我们内部有一个「星眠设定手册」 ，这个东西很重要，我觉得它是个基础。一旦我们有了这个东西，文案、AI训练、策划和程序就有了一套话语体系，就能拉齐标准 ， 我们内部就能有一套协同的机制去做这件事 。
新知：在商业化方面，CEO张月光之前在公开场合分享称，《星眠》想采用游戏化的商业模式而不是卖token，但从二测来看，《星眠》似乎也准备了售卖对话次数的付费方式？
何泪泪：二测其实核心想尝试的不是把AI当做独立的商品来定价，而是把它嵌入游戏既有的商业循环中间， 让AI功能和抽卡这种传统的付费点运行在同一套经济循环体系之下 。现在看来可能还需要再优化一下，怎么让这个 （卖token的） 感觉少一点。
AI陪伴卖token不是好的商业模式。我们肯定是希望用一些成熟的商业化逻辑来承载这些AI功能，玩家是通过日常资源分配自己参与进来，不去单独为AI资源买单。
活跃任务、材料副本都接近传统乙游的资源模式
我们也想观察一下用户对这种模式的接受度，通过用户资源分配的数据，反过来帮助我们优化一下之后的付费模型，让AI在里面是一种渗透关系。我不希望AI是单独拎出来的。我刚刚也讲到了用场景化来解决关系问题，所以我希望是 场景因为有了AI的加持，让玩家跟星眠的关系更好了，然后玩家自己决定愿不愿意为此而付费 。
我觉得这件事情会带来一个认知层上的变化。传统乙游是体力容易获取、容易囤积，玩家对它的价值感可能会模糊一点。那么在AI功能和卡池付费统一的情况下， 玩家会不会重新理解游戏的货币体系和分配逻辑，更愿意去体验这个场景和场景中间AI所带来的感受 。 这确实也是我们想验证的，而不是单独地卖token。
这是第一部分，第一步是商业化验证，除了用游戏化去包装之外，能不能去加持传统乙游的商业模式，如果能加持那挺好的。
第二个部分是它有没有可能 降低一下乙游的宣发成本 。现在流量越来越贵，但《星眠》因为有AI的加入，现在小红书上大家发帖的内容除了传统乙游的那些卡面漂亮、文案写得好之外，还有很多人是分享AI弹幕的，跟星眠聊天的内容的，还有星眠的日记，等等。这些小的亮点都是契机，让用户可以分享，然后吸引更多人。 这个模式已经验证了是可以降低宣发成本的 ，如果用传统KOC的模式去引发这么大的讨论量，得花很多钱了。
这两块验证了之后，我们会有下一步的验证，就是想看一下通过AI的加持做关系来把IP立住了之后，从内容消费变成关系入口之后，有没有可能 诞生新的商业模式，比如跟硬件、跟具身智能去做结合，然后变成新的流量入口 。
举个例子，跟星眠熟了他更懂你 （玩家） 了之后，你和他说我杯子摔了，要买个杯子，星眠可能会给你发个链接，说这个杯子很适合你，这个颜色或者样式你喜欢，然后这上面还有只猫跟你家猫长得一样——这个转化率肯定是高的。
新知：二测到目前为止，玩家对这套数值体系的反馈如何？
何泪泪：因为我们二测还没有开付费，所以只能通过用户对体力的分配和用户反馈来观察，目前基本都是正向的评价。这会给我们更多的信心去接着去做这个事。
新知：未来除了模拟经营之外，还会加入新的玩法吗？
何泪泪：会的。但模拟经营肯定是主循环的最核心的玩法，是为了推动数值、推动目标感的，这是不会变的。在这个基础上，像刚才说的，我们会去做和AI的结合，然后会加很多东西去为陪伴提供场景、激活长期关系。其他一些玩法也在规划中，不过会通过AI更互动化。
新知：现在能看到已上线的和在研的乙游、AI陪伴产品，有不少都是3D风格的。《星眠》为什么选用的是2D风格？会不会担心在这方面有竞争压力？
何泪泪：这个问题我们之前也想过。我以前做过女性研究，那个时候就有一个想法，就是我 （玩家） 和男主到底是什么样的时空交互逻辑。我觉得好多AI陪伴产品是选择让他来到我的世界，但 《星眠》的选择是让我去他的世界 。
这是不一样的。他来到我的世界这件事，我觉得不是特别成立。我的世界是现实世界，是没有办法用各种东西去证明他的价值的。 因为实际上，他来到我们的世界这件事，可能就是需要像穿越小说一样，他真的在现实世界获得真实身体和身份体验才算真正做到。实际上现在的情况，在一个游戏里这件事是不成立的。玩家总会觉得他不知道很多现实的事情，而想要让他知道的事，其实每个人的需求也不同。
但是我想做的是让用户去他的世界，这个时候逻辑就变了。因为他的世界是游戏世界，游戏可以用声光电服化道来烘托他，来告诉用户这个人非常值得你爱，因为他在那个世界的价值判断体系里是值得被爱的。这样在长久的亲密关系里面就平等了，是非常适合去建立关系的。
有了这个前提之后，再讲3D和2D的区别。3D就是写实，会太像在我 （玩家） 的身边了，太像把他拉来我的世界这个状态了。 但是2D最大化地保证了一定的幻想性，还有画风的差异化。 2D美术其实有不可替代的优势，它可以非常细微地呈现出人物的差异和个性化。简单来说，现实中哪找得到一个瞳孔是黄蓝渐变的人。
所以我是从理念出发，就是到底我想构筑一个什么样的状态，我觉得是需要用户去他的世界，所以2D在这方面是有优势的。而且我们在Live2D上的演绎其实属于相当优秀的水准了。所以结合来看，我还是比较偏向于选择2D。
有丰富的神态和动作变化，说话时口型还能和语音对应上
技术上「全是难题」
新知：《星眠》被很多玩家喜欢的一个特色，是触摸互动的时候可以得到非预设的、即时生成的、不重复的回复。这个功能在技术上是如何实现的？
何泪泪：触摸反馈其实是agent管线共同协同的作用。这个功能也还有一些没实现的部分，就是刚才说的context之间互相串联的功能，用户行为应该对AI有影响，比如刚给他换了套新衣服，再去首页摸他，回应应该是不一样的。我们未来着力要去做的就是串联，把所有的信息串起来，会让他的火热感更重一些，更有沉浸感，这种无处不在的爱就更重一些。
除了这个之外，技术上还有一些 （专门的设计） 。比如我们会有 不同的管线 去解决用户在不同场景下产生的体验需求。在聊天上通过文风、记忆度、回答时机等不同方式，都做出了不同的约束。以此来约束星眠不能ooc和做出脱离角色设定的行为。
这方面我经过了大量的调研，发现用户对于ooc这件事的判断比较直观，会涉及到 说话方式及口头习惯等情况。所以我们会有很多方式去限定它， 当限定情况做到了一定的颗粒度 ，就能最大化地让用户有这种设定的稳定感。
还有以上我讲到的所有的东西，其实最后是需要进行台词承接的，包括触摸反馈和AVG反馈，都需要上下文的承接，这个也要去 润色 ，所以其实 又是一个管线 。相当于其实开了thinking，过程中有非常多背后的思考，但是用户不知道。
新知：但是实际体验过程中，这些thinking的过程感受不到任何卡顿，这是怎么实现的？
何泪泪：因为有很多分步的过程，不是所有东西都要同步过这些管线的。对话的管线就不会那么复杂，因为需要实时回应，就需要很快。但如果是日记和AVG里的体验，它就可以多thinking一下，反正又不是马上要产出。一般我们拉长时间的场景，管线就会复杂一些。
新知：这个过程中遇到过什么技术难题吗？
何泪泪： 全是难题。 （笑） 它其实是这样的，一条叫设计线，一条叫反验线。
设计线来讲，AI这一块肯定是从源头设计需求，逻辑判断，然后把这个事情先跑通， （保证） 起码它逻辑是通的，这件事是能实现的。然后就要进入评测状态了。
反验线就是测完了之后，一定会发现最开始的一些逻辑的细节是跑不通的，比如说串联什么的出现问题。那肯定需要通过别的方式去调整，来保证这个东西顺畅。这是一种反验，就是内部反验。
新知：刚才您提到《星眠》用的是自研模型，这是一开始就决定好的吗？
何泪泪：对，这个事情涉及到两个方面。一方面是成本比较可控，因为我们不是大模型，我们是小模型，是一个陪伴模型，就只是针对于陪伴这个场景所产出的模型。它需要的样本量没有那么大，训练成本也不会那么高。
比如提醒生理期这件事，如果像日历一样提醒你，你并不会觉得这是什么关系上的感知。和现在女生不喜欢听到多喝热水是一样的，我们希望自研模型更往情感承接上做努力。
大模型目前发展但是极其迅速的，迭代很快，每一次迭代我们都需要重新适配，对创业团队来说是比较难的事情。 另一方面也是我们想在情感陪伴模型上更加 专 精一些。
我们综合考虑了使用场景、需求、成本，肯定是先基于各个场景积累用户的数据资源，然后训练增强我们自己的模型在对应场景的效果。 我觉得从现在的成果来看，开源加自有数据训练，其实是有可能超越一些模型在特定场景的效果的。 因为大模型还是太泛了。
玩家对自研模型的交流能力比较认可
团队不到百人，招人太难了
新知：您以前主要是在做互联网产品，这是第一次接触游戏研发，做的过程中能感觉到思路有什么不一样吗？
何泪泪：我感觉不太一样的地方是在于，游戏行业已经发展了二十年很成熟的工作模式。
我虽然是游戏制作人，同时也是《星眠》的AI训练负责人，我因为之前的一些工作经历，在AI上会比较有经验。AI训练这一块从构思开始，跟游戏可能就不太一样了。它当然也会去做用户调研，了解用户的诉求在哪里，但是我们 更多地还得考虑到AI能力的边界 ，然后要把AI能力的边界和用户的诉求更好地结合起来。
比如用户希望剧情能够千人千面，但其实有两个方面会限制它。一方面是如果真的千人千面，其实非常考验用户的创造力，用户得自带剧情，这是一件很难的事。第二方面就是一旦剧情千人千面，也非常考验AI的能力。AI在创意上我觉得还是比较「抽卡」。它不能保证所有东西都是最好的。
新知：各个部门协作的时候，是AI这边在主导决策，还是游戏这边在主导决策？
何泪泪：我们其实不以职能划边界，是以方向划边界。比如刚才说到AI对AVG设计、对玩法、对与AI native有关的游戏设计都有提升，这三个的发起是不太一样的。AVG方面文案会占主导多一点，文案写了什么东西AI再配合去做。玩法这块策划会主导多一点，AI native这块就是AI训练主导多一点。
然后因为团队规模也不是特别大，我们就以目标结果为导向，控进度，拿结果。我们脑暴完之后，哪方发起的需求，其他几方在一个项目节奏里对齐目标、验证、交付，是这样去做协同。
新知：跨界到游戏之后，组建团队的过程会比较困难吗？
何泪泪：是的。找人也分为两块，AI类的人和游戏类的人。AI类的人除了技术要过硬，在陪伴和娱乐领域也要对用户有了解，知道女生的关注点在哪里。还需要有把用户需求量化或者抽象出来的能力，这是在AI方向很需要的能力，需要对用户有深刻的洞察。还需要能把AI技术转化来真正增强乙女游戏体验的能力。这些都是AI方面招人比较难的地方。
游戏招人比较难的地方，一是在于对AI游戏赛道需要认可，需要对这件事感兴趣。因为我还是希望一个团队能够大家都喜欢在做的事，这样才有好的创新。然后还有一个客观原因，就是北京的游戏公司真的很少，特别是女性向的，这一块我们也是非常麻烦棘手的，不算特别顺利。
新知：目前团队大致是怎样的规模？
何泪泪： 现在不到百人 ，应该是非常精简了，因为我们招人真的很严。还是那句话，我希望是一群志同道合的人把这件事走下去，团队每一个人都是高度自治的。 一测的时候人还要更少，不到50人。 我们扩充也蛮克制的，因为人多不一定好办事。
新知：团队未来如果继续扩充，会主要扩充什么方向？
何泪泪：会比较侧重于AI。现在公司里按方向划分人数，游戏比AI的比例应该是3:1。
新知：您认为AI陪伴游戏目前处于什么发展阶段？
何泪泪：我觉得现在比较早期，还大有可为。我也讲过了《星眠》设计AI的三个方向，也讲到了未来跳出游戏框架可能的商业模式的探索。因为我们用AI加持了用户关系，有了关系之后，关系的变现是没有天花板的。我觉得现在挑战也会有，机遇也会存在。《星眠》的产品形态还有很多提升空间，可以拭目以待。
从市场需求来讲，我真的觉得永远有机会，因为市场永远是喜新厌旧的。AI的加入又带来了构建关系的整个过程，这个关系还能更长久。
新知：现在用户会不会对AI还存在一些疑虑和抵触情绪？
何泪泪：这个事情我想得很清楚，所以我们说「人工筑IP，AI养关系」。我觉得不管是用户的接受程度还是IP的精良度，肯定人工是最好的，这件事是一定不会变的，我们AI是绝不参与 剧情、美术、音乐等需要人创作力的事情的 。
我觉得从《星眠》的二测反馈来看， 用户对AI促关系这件事反馈很好 。一测的时候我们体量还比较小，吸引来的用户比较偏向AI聊天。但是二测已经触达到乙游的一些核心用户了，大家还是蛮惊喜的。所以我觉得用户更在意的是你用不用心，最直观的表现就是图够不够精细认真、是不是人工画的。
/   END   /

title: Krafton shuts down PUBG spin-off Black Budget nine months after closed alpha test
text:
Krafton is ending development on PUBG spin-off Black Budget nine months after its closed alpha test on Steam.
Black Budget is an extraction shooter built around a time loop, with the goal of having whole teams survive and escape rather than a last-one-standing battle royale. Black Budget held several alpha and community tests throughout the year.
"After reviewing the project's development status and future direction, we concluded that its current direction would not allow us to deliver an experience players could enjoy over the long term," Krafton posted to Steam .
"We sincerely thank everyone who took the time to participate in our Closed Alpha tests and share their feedback. PUBG Studios will carry what we learned from development and testing into future projects, continuing to listen to players as we explore new gameplay experiences."
Black Budget was the second PUBG spin-off to be cancelled this year. In March, Krafton shut down the free-to-play spin-off Blindspot after two months in Early Access.
Krafton previously outlined its plan to expand PUBG Battlegrounds into a "content platform" with "sandbox-oriented UGC that leverages PUBG's core gunplay, mechanics, and physics engine, consolidating an ecosystem where players can create and share their own content."
It had said that Black Budget and Blindspot would "test the PUBG IP's expansion into new genres, while new platform advancements will bring PUBG to the next step for growth."
Despite the two cancellations, PUBG announced another spin-off at Gamescom in August called PUBG: Ded.Net, a multiplayer shooter with roguelike progression.
Krafton reported record Q2 results , with revenue increasing 94.9% to ₩1.29 trillion ($889.1 million). The company attributed this growth to the continued expansion of the PUBG franchise and the success of Unknown Worlds' Subnautica 2.
PUBG revenue increased 25% year-over-year, driven by the development of a central gameplay platform and new "cultural collaborations" with other IP and brands.

title: 2XKO would have needed an MAU base "in the high hundreds of thousands, if not millions" to succeed
text:
Riot Games' 2XKO would have had to attract a base of monthly active users "in the high hundreds of thousands, if not millions" to be sustainable, according to CPO Marc Merrill.
On The Lemonade Stand podcast (as spotted by IGN ), Riot's co-founder and co-chairman stated that although the game resonated with some players, the audience was "not nearly enough" to support the game's intended live service model.
2XKO ended active development in August , as it cost "substantially more to operate than it [brought] in, and engagement stayed relatively flat despite larger updates."
The game is still playable and free to download on PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X|S, with servers remaining online "beyond 2026."
In addition to the need for a large player base, Merrill cited the release of Street Fighter 6 as a factor in 2XKO's unsuccessful launch.
"I think we had a window to do some great things to really help the fighting game community, and then Street Fighter 6 came out, which was something like eight years after we started working on 2XKO," Merrill explained.
"We had an awesome development team of really talented people that did great work and made a beautiful game. We'd already communicated all this stuff to players, and so we were like, 'You know what? Let's keep going, let's give it to the community. Let's see what happens."
He added: "I think if we came out, ideally when we should've, years before Street Fighter, I think we would have made a really significant impact."
Merrill also discussed Riot's 2016 acquisition of Radiant Entertainment, noting that its free-to-play title Rising Thunder, released in alpha in 2015, was a major inspiration for 2XKO.
After acquiring Radiant Entertainment, Riot removed Rising Thunder from storefronts and eventually cancelled it, but released it as open-source a year later .
Merrill explained that Riot aimed to combine Rising Thunder's "simple controls and cool concept relating to a 1v1 fighting game" with "the League IP with the Cannon brothers, and add a cool Riot-style competitive ecosystem," which led to the creation of 2XKO.
However, leadership changes resulted in a lack of "alignment on the strategy, which then caused managerial fracturing." Merrill noted that the team received conflicting guidance and concluded, "We've got nobody to blame but ourselves."

title: Reigns developer Nerial closes following "significant trading losses" over past two years
text:
Reigns and Card Shark developer Nerial has announced its closure as it enters "hibernation mode."
In a statement on social media , studio founders CEO Tamara Alliot and creative director François Alliot said that "after 13 years and 11 published games, we have decided together with our partners at Devolver to end development and the studio."
Devolver acquired Nerial in 2021 . Last year, the team was reduced by 40% to "address issues around recent releases and to better shape the team for future releases."
François told Kotaku that Devolver will retain the rights to Nerial's existing catalogue, and emphasised that they remain "very good friends."
"Having been bought by Devolver, you become an internal studio, so that means each of our games needs to be a Devolver game," he noted. "And Devolver needs to publish all Nerial games, which it did match very well for Reigns, it did match very well for Card Shark, for example. So there is this common ground and we would have found a way."
"But it's like, every time we have to think about what the other wants. And there's a bit of a second-guessing. I recognise this situation, where you lose a bit of the concentrated energy that you had as a pure indie. And I want to get back to that in some way… it might work, might not work, but it doesn't involve so many people."
Games journalist Chris Kerr noted that a recent Companies House fiscal report indicated the studio experienced two years of "significant trading losses" and had become "dependent" on financial support from Devolver. Nerial lost over £800,000 in 2025 and nearly £1 million in 2024.
Nerial has nine employees, including its founders. Tamara and François stated they plan to continue making games and "return to [their] roots," but will first "take a break and reflect on everything that's happened, before coming back with a new perspective."
"The fabulous Nerial team will now seek new opportunities and we wholeheartedly recommend each and every one to any potential studios that will be lucky enough to have them."
François told Kotaku that "he hopes to be able to continue to work with them as contractors in the future, but isn’t currently in a position to retain them as salaried employees"
"We also want to thank the many amazing people we've teamed up with, both inside the studio, at Devolver, and through ad hoc collaborations. Each of our projects was only possible through such impossible, fleeting conjunctions of talent and passion."
François said that he needed to "step back and rethink what I want to do with my indie career."
"It's become a bit difficult to push forward, especially with the current context, with post-COVID, there's a bit of this crash in the video game industry that everyone knows. AI sucking out all the air from the room. So we are rebuilding, trying to rebuild strong roots. And for that, I need to take a step back."

title: Winners of the UK Best Places To Work Awards 2026 revealed
text:
The UK Best Places to Work Awards 2026 took place at the Royal Institution in London on October 1, with special awards going to Dink, Hangar 13, Jagex: The RuneScape Company, NaturalMotion Games, Rare, and Snap Finger Click.
The awards ceremony took place after the GamesIndustry.biz HR Summit, which was attended by 79 representatives from 41 companies, including AAA, AA, and indie studios, as well as consultancy firms, training providers, and educational institutes.
The main Best Places to Work awards recognised a total of 25 firms across three categories – small, mid-sized, and large companies – for their excellence in supporting staff. These awards are judged on the basis of an employee survey (worth 80% of the score) and a company survey (worth 20%).
The Best Places to Work Awards 2026 was sponsored by Amiqus, Playground Games, IO Interactive, Games London, and Special Effect.
“What makes these events especially valuable is how well they complement each other," said Liz Prince MBE, Business Manager at Amiqus. "The HR Summit creates space for honest discussions, shared learning and new ideas, while the Best Places To Work Awards shine a spotlight on the studios and businesses that are turning those ideas into action. Bringing the industry together to both learn from each other and celebrate success helps raise standards for everyone, and we're proud to play a part in that.”
“We’re proud to support GI.Biz in recognising the UK’s best mid-sized Video Game Studios," said Paul Evans, Director of HR & Recruitment at Playground Games. "These are not only teams that are creating brilliant games, but studios who are also setting the standard for what a great place to work looks like in our industry”.
Hangar 13 UK | Image credit: GamesIndustry.biz
The winner of this year's G Into Gaming award was Jo Haslam, currently Design Director at Snap Finger Click following a long career at Mediatonic, Relentless and the BBC. Liz Prince MBE presented the award, describing Haslam as "one of those rare people who leads with both empathy and action in perfect unison," and "an inspiring woman and a natural leader." Snap Finger Click also left with both a Best Places to Work Award and this year's Diversity Award.
Rare once again took the Environmental Award, sponsored by Games London, while Middlesborough indie Dink won the Education Award, presented by IO Interactive Chief Development Officer Veronique Lallier.

title: Bungie co-founder and Destiny 2 narrative director launch transmedia studio Stone Kite
text:
Bungie co-founder Jason Jones and Destiny 2 narrative director Margaret Stohl have launched a new transmedia studio called Stone Kite.
Jones co-created the Halo and Destiny franchises, while Stohl worked on several video games and co-founded 7 Studios with Lewis Paterson, which Activision later acquired. She is CEO of Stone Kite, and is also the author of the Beautiful Creatures series.
Described as a "world-building studio," the Los Angeles-based Stone Kite is debuting with its first IP, One Zero One, adapted from an original manuscript by Jones.
One Zero One centres on "a coming worldwide conflict between humanity and a rogue army of AI-driven robotic soldiers" and will launch as a four-part comic book series. New issues will be released online for free in early 2027, followed by additional media projects.
Stone Kite's founding team includes former media SVP Stephen Wacker, president Lewis Peterson, film and TV VP Matt Johnson, and narrative creative director Jeanine Schaefer.
Stone Kite is collaborating with more than 250 creators from across the entertainment industry, including director and producer Jay Roach, comic book writer and artist Christian Ward, illustrator Kyle Lambert, author Stephen Graham Jones, and screenwriter Akela Cooper.
"I've spent my career creating books, games, comics, film and television, and I've seen how often the medium that tells the first story ends up defining everything that comes after it," said Stohl.
"Stone Kite is about breaking down those old media silos. Instead of starting in one medium and adapting outward, we bring the best global creators from different disciplines into the room from day one to shape the world together."
Jason Jones added: "I used to bike fifteen miles along Lake Michigan to the used bookstores in North Chicago, and bike home again with a backpack full of sci-fi paperbacks. Margie was the first person to believe I could write a book of my own, the first person to read it, and the one person I trusted to help me develop it into epic entertainment that leaves the world a better place."

title: "Quite often it's given me more to do" – Why AI might be creating more work for games companies, rather than saving time
text:
The GamesIndustry.biz HR Summit took place on October 1, and one topic that came up again and again at sessions throughout the day was generative AI and the impact it's having on the workplace.
Attitudes towards the technology were mixed. Some pointed to how AI has been able to speed up some aspects of the game creation process, such as coding, or automate drudge work. But the general view was that generative AI falls far short of the miracle cure that some AI enthusiasts pitch it as, and that in addition it has been causing all sorts of workplace problems as firms figure out how best to use and account for it – including worries about the privacy of sensitive company data, an increase in employee anxiety, and a higher workload for HR professionals as a result of lengthy AI-written grievance letters.
One senior leader emphasised that their company was meticulous about not letting any AI-generated content end up in a finished game (the HR Summit ran under the Chatham House Rule ). But at the same time, their company recognises AI might have uses elsewhere. "So it's a fine balance," they said, acknowledging that "there could be good opportunities for efficiencies and doing some of the more routine jobs or mundane jobs that we never want to do in game development."
The GamesIndustry.biz HR Summit took place at The Royal Institution in London | Image credit: GamesIndustry.biz
Yet there remains huge anxiety among employees about the use of AI, they warned: "I've had emails from people at nine o'clock at night going, 'Are we using AI? Oh my God, does that mean my job's going to go?'" That anxiety extends to management teams, which worry about where the tech is going and how to plan for it. "The reality is that we don't know what the future is going to look like," said another senior leader.
At last year's HR Summit, a show of hands revealed that only a minority of attendees' companies had an AI policy in place. This year, a similar straw poll revealed that most now have an AI policy. But the sheer speed of change is causing headaches. "I wrote a policy two weeks ago, and then I found out about some prompt injection yesterday that means I've got to go back and rewrite some of the guidelines," said one company leader. "It's changing that quick."
Related
Saber Interactive's chief creative officer says "We've never replaced anybody with AI"
Tim Willits responds to accusations that a writer was replaced with ChatGPT
One of the biggest worries is sensitive data leaking outside the company. Even if firms pay for an enterprise version of an AI model that ensures none of the company's data is used for training by the AI firm, they have little control over employees' individual use of AI models. "They could be going off to ChatGPT on their personal account and putting all sorts of NDA things in there. And I don't see how you can physically stop people doing that," said one leader. "So being a bit clearer about what we think is acceptable and unacceptable, that's the best way forward."
"I haven't seen AI create anything fun"
Yet there's still confusion about exactly how AI should be used. "The biggest issue at the minute is that AI is the answer, but people don't quite know what the question is," said one leader, who described multiple studios seeking to "use more AI" without a clear idea of what they want it to do.
"We're in this kind of over-hyped world. We're all hoping that this great panacea is going to open up, it's going to be amazing. And like every other advance, it's not."
One senior-level attendee summed it up bluntly: "I haven't seen AI create anything fun. It can replicate, for sure, but I haven't seen anything fun come from AI yet."
"You can make crap quicker," quipped another.
AI workflows
Whatever your attitude towards AI, the message at the HR Summit was clear: you can't ignore it. Even if your company doesn't want to use generative AI in any form, that needs to be enshrined in employee guidelines and enforced, and everyone needs to keep up with what's going on.
Related
European game developers are more concerned that AI will pressure them to work faster rather than take their job
Games industry employment survey finds half of respondents are worried AI could reduce work quality, while 46% say AI makes it harder to assess actual skills
"It's really about understanding what the current state of AI technology is, understanding how that aligns with the values of your organisation, how it aligns with the people of your organisation, and the risks and opportunities that then creates," said one speaker. "AI technologies are now encroaching on a lot of creative disciplines that five years ago we did not even consider would be an issue."
Yet we're only really at the start of the generative AI journey. One session outlined the four stages of AI adoption, from dabbling with AI to becoming an AI-first company. The vast majority of companies are still at the first stage, perhaps buying an enterprise license for Claude to let programmers play around with generating code. But a lot of larger studios are in stage two, where they are trialling generative AI in certain workflows, evaluating the time savings against the potential cost and risk.
"There were more fingers than most humans have on this particular piece of art"
Without rigid enforcement, however, chaos can ensue. One attendee provided an anecdote about an artist using Gemini to generate some shader code while a programmer was out of the office. The inefficient code, which didn't conform to the company's coding standard and went against the studio's terms and conditions on generative AI, was only spotted weeks later, and resulted in the build being reverted.
Another anecdote involved outsourcing a piece of art to a freelancer, who used AI to create it. "There were more fingers than most humans have," said one speaker. "But another person outside of that department went, 'That looks great, ship it', and the community went absolutely wild. So that time and cost saving they thought they got wasn't there."
AI workflow pilots can also reveal fatal flaws in studio processes. "Most of them collapse, because [workflows are] driven by the tacit knowledge of individuals rather than formally documented operating procedures," said a speaker.
There's also the human side to consider. Even if an AI-driven workflow allows programmers to submit more code more efficiently, they said, "we also have to look at it from the qualitative side. Yes, you're able to move faster, but did this improve the quality of the process for the people involved? Because a lot of the times we move faster, but it was a miserable experience: 'I spent most of it just shouting at an AI prompt thing that I couldn't quite get to do what I wanted it to do'."
HR headache
From an HR perspective, a few of the summit's attendees pointed to how generative AI can be beneficial. In terms of writing emails, "sometimes AI is really great for helping people frame up what they really want to say," said one attendee. "Sometimes you just need a bit of a prompt or a kick just to get your thoughts in order." AI-based HR systems can also provide automatic answers to commonly asked questions about things like maternity or sickness leave.
But AI is also generating more work. Several people pointed to an increase in employees using generative AI to write grievance letters, which can be many, many pages long. One legal representative said they receive around ten such letters from clients every week. "They generally go long, with quite a lot of factual detail that isn't quite correct, and often the legal references are quite odd."
"Eight pages of it contained things that we couldn't even make sense of"
The problem is that HR representatives are dutybound to faithfully read and respond to these lengthy AI-written grievances, even if they cite incorrect information or make irrelevant claims. "It's not doing any favours for the claimant either," said one attendee. It was noted that if the employee can't show that they understand the details of the AI-generated report, the case could be thrown out by a tribunal.
"We had one not long ago, and it was a grievance an employee submitted, a formal one, about nine pages long – and probably eight pages of it contained things that we couldn't even make sense of," said one attendee. "Bear in mind, it's just the first stage of the formal grievance on something that was actually relatively minor that could have been sorted out between myself and the line manager and the employee."
Yet the solution isn't as simple as simply banning AI-authored letters of complaint – as one attendee pointed out, some employees might need support with writing, and banning AI use could be seen as discriminatory. But another attendee suggested a potential solution of sorts by adjusting the company's policy to stipulate a maximum word count for grievance letters, or responding with a request for specific timelines, dates, and details that an AI wouldn't know, rather than spending hours with the legal team trying to decipher the complaint.
On balance, it seems like generative AI could actually be generating more work for HR teams. "The reality of it is that we've had HR teams that have shrunk, but the amount of work that you have has stayed the same or gone up," said one attendee. "And just because people are using AI or using LLMs to try and help these things, actually quite often it's given me more to do."
"It doesn't have heart. It can't read the person"
They pointed out that providing AI-generated replies to common HR questions might mean HR representatives are missing the essential human connection with the employees they're charged with helping. "Because the person who asked about the maternity policy might be having to go through IVF and they need some additional support, but they just found the answers out without realising there are a million other things that we can do for them as well. They're asking about the sickness policy because somebody needed to go and have an operation in a hospital, and they were worried that they weren't going to get paid for the time that they needed for the recovery."
The AI can answer the question, but it can't provide empathy or pick up on emotional cues, they concluded. "It doesn't have heart. It can't read the person. It can't tell what else might be going on. It can't feel the vibe in the room when you walk in, or see someone's body language."
"That connection with people is the glue that brings it all together."

title: In pictures: the Best Places To Work Awards 2026
text:
Last night saw the reveal of this year's GamesIndustry.biz Best Places To Work Awards UK , which returned to the Royal Institution in London at the end of the GamesIndustry.biz HR Summit. title: Sony's consultation on physical media: better late than never | Opinion
text:
The news that Sony is surveying its development partners to get their input on its decision to end support for physical game releases ( first reported by Moore's Law is Dead ) is a little odd, at least from a sequencing perspective. You'd generally imagine that talking to your most important business partners would be something to be done before making a major public announcement of an enormous change that will impact all of them. Better late than never, I suppose, though exactly how much better remains to be seen.
What this belated consultation hammers home is just how unilateral the decision to end physical game distribution has been. It's not that it was a particularly surprising decision – it always looked likely that physical media support in the next generation of console hardware would be an afterthought at best. It was, however, a poorly handled one. There were ways to do this that showed more flexibility and encouraged more buy-in from both industry partners and consumers; it didn't have to be quite so high-handed.
The consultation, for all that it amounts to conducting a listening exercise about barn door security long after the horse has bolted, suggests that Sony is realising it may have overstepped somewhat. I don't think it will result in much of a change to the company's announced policy – the timing makes it feel more like a PR sop to the unexpectedly strident backlash the policy has received than a genuine reconsideration, though some additional flexibility (perhaps allowing companies to optionally do physical releases for the rest of the PS5's lifespan, for instance) might end up being put forward as a compromise.
There were ways to do this that showed more flexibility and encouraged more buy-in from both industry partners and consumers
That would be something, I suppose, though it doesn't change the medium- to long-term calculus of the decision, and is unlikely to really quiet down the opposition to it. Sony appears to have been slightly blindsided by the vehemence of that opposition; its announcement, and I suspect the received wisdom within the company's own corridors, hinged on the understanding that physical sales are such a small and shrinking portion of the market that hardly anyone would care about that side of things being quietly shut down. There would always be some die-hards, but by and large I imagine that the people in charge of the decision at Sony expected to be able to record an hour of death for disc-based media without much fanfare.
The extent to which consumers are upset about the decision likely exceeds what Sony expected – but the extent to which some pretty prominent industry figures have come out to publicly express disappointment about the decision absolutely wasn't part of the plan. A lot of the disagreement comes down to personal preference for physical media, of course, but there's also a really strong current here – especially in the comments from developers and publishing executives – that implies that Sony has overlooked, or perhaps simply disregarded, a really genuine commercial concern about this decision as well.
Related
Sony clarifies re-order support for existing PlayStation discs
Platform holder adds the process for ordering discs will change as it shifts to an all-digital future
The idea that digital game sales are simply steadily displacing physical game sales in a clean, linear fashion is, after all, vastly too simplistic. Nobody can deny that digital distribution is now the dominant mode on consoles, just as it has been on PCs for decades, but the role that digital and physical games play within the commercial ecosystem isn't a straight one-to-one swap. Consumers with a clear preference for one form or the other certainly exist, but a mixture of both formats is pretty common as well – with physical game purchases occupying notably more of the market at both the high-value and low-value extremes.
Sony has overlooked, or perhaps simply disregarded, a really genuine commercial concern about this decision
The low-value aspect is well understood, and has been an argument within the industry for a move to digital distribution for more than a quarter of a century now. Physical games can be resold by consumers, creating a second-hand market that holds prices down and provides excellent value for frugal gamers (often younger consumers or those with less disposable income). Without physical games, that low-cost end of the market will dry up; pricing power will lie entirely in the hands of Sony and the publishers.
The high-value aspect of physical media, however, is also very important and seems to have been largely overlooked in Sony's decision-making. For a lot of gamers, digital game purchases are the workhorse – month-to-month subscription payments or picking up digital games when they're on sale or otherwise discounted. Physical purchases, meanwhile, are special. They might be preorders for major games they've been looking forward to, often with a special edition or pre-order bonus of some kind; or in the case of many indie titles, limited edition physical runs aimed at the game's biggest fans.
Related
"We are profoundly disappointed by Sony's decision" – Game companies express dismay at the end of PlayStation disc production
Atari, Iam8bit, Lost in Cult, and Silver Linings Interactive are among the firms lamenting the loss of physical games
This separation isn't specific to games – it's found across every form of media right now. In an era of Spotify and Apple Music, more and more people are opting to buy vinyl records (and lately, even cassettes). They're a tiny sliver of the market compared to Spotify listeners, but a pretty solid chunk of the revenue for many musicians and smaller labels. Special editions of books in beautiful bindings and slipcases do remarkably well despite the convenience of e-readers. High-quality releases of movies on 4K Blu-Rays, meanwhile, remain a lucrative sideline for Hollywood – enough so that restorations and remasters of classic movies often get a limited theatrical release largely designed to promote the physical media release itself.
It's smaller titles and publishers that often do the best from physical distribution if measured by revenue percentages
A key thing to note here is that the value of physical media is unevenly distributed. It doesn't matter a great deal to a big blockbuster or an artist doing billions of streams on Spotify; but to a niche movie or artist with a loyal following, or a smaller label or studio, physical releases can add up to a massive part of their business. The same holds true for videogames. While major titles can earn a solid amount of revenue from physical sales in spite of their being a relatively small percentage in unit terms, it's smaller titles and publishers that often do the best from physical distribution if measured by revenue percentages.
Of course, it's possible to sell a special or collectors' edition of a game online – most games at least attempt to do this – but with the exception of bundling a DLC season pass or something along those lines, the actual value and appeal of those editions is questionable. It's obvious to everyone involved, after all, that a "collectors' edition" you buy digitally isn't actually being "collected" in any way; and if you had any doubts to that end, media companies including Sony quite regularly pop up in courtrooms to make the blunt argument that consumers don't actually own their digital purchases at all. That doesn't matter too much to the average consumer buying something from the PlayStation Store – one could argue that it should matter more, but it's obvious that it's not a consideration for most. For a devoted fan with a collector's mindset and deep pockets to match, though, it's anathema.
Sony's mind is unlikely to be changed, at least by anything short of the baleful eye of regulators in the EU or elsewhere falling on what's about to be something that looks awfully like exactly the kind of walled garden that Apple, Google and others were recently forced to open up to the world. The PS6 (and Microsoft's next-gen Xbox) are very unlikely to support any kind of physical media; if they wanted to, they could at least have copied Nintendo's game-key cartridge approach (which gives consumers a physical asset that can be loaned or resold, even if the game data itself resides in the cloud), but the will to do that clearly doesn't exist.
Every other medium has held on to an element of physical distribution, valuable in its capacity to cultivate super-fans as much as for its revenue
Yet for all that Sony might have expected this change to pass without much fuss, the reality is that it will leave games – the youngest of the major entertainment media – in a unique and not entirely favourable position. Every other medium has held on to an element of physical distribution; vestigial, certainly, but lucrative in a way that punches beyond its weight, and valuable in its capacity to cultivate super-fans as much as for its revenue streams. Within a few short years, the only equivalent of that for videogames may indeed be Nintendo's key-cards. The industry would have thrown away an entire segment of its business largely on what appears to be a technical whim, and with minimal proper discussion of what value that segment holds and what might be lost by its passing.
The fact that some kind of consultation may now finally be happening at least suggests an understanding that this is a big decision, not just a change to be made casually. What opportunities to change path actually remain at this point is unclear, but at least we're going to have some kind of conversation about the ratio of baby to bathwater that's being thrown out with physical media.
If nothing else, the voices of publishers and developers who have spent years figuring out how to boost their games' revenues by offering desirable special and limited editions to their most dedicated fans should be heard. The best time to hear those voices would have been before pulling the rug out from underneath them; but listening now could at least offer chances to soften the blow.

title: 'Xbox is not for sale,' CEO Asha Sharma says
text:
The new CEO said made a particular proclamation while speaking with New York Times.
Amid Microsoft's ongoing struggles with Xbox, the gaming division is not for sale, according to CEO Asha Sharma. Sharma said as much in an interview with the New York Times on Wednesday .
"Xbox is not for sale," Sharma said. "We will do whatever it takes to set the company up for success, and we will look at the right partnerships, the right operating model, and everything needed to achieve that."
A report from The Information in June said Microsoft didn't have immediate plans to spin off Xbox, but that the company "hasn't ruled out spinning out or restructuring the unit as a wholly-owned subsidiary, which could make it easier to sell, or creating a joint venture with other partners." The Information report cited this information to three people with direct knowledge.
Rumors have subsisted since then, but Sharma's comments suggest rumors of a sale are wrong. Her comments, however, do not rule out Microsoft restructuring the company to operate more like LinkedIn, for instance. Microsoft has owned LinkedIn since 2016, but it operated independently as a subsidiary.
Related: Reigns developer Nerial enters 'hibernation mode,' lays off staff
Developers looking for new insight on Sharma's strategy may come away short-changed, as much of her insights from the profile echoed previous statements. "All I can do is look at it from a first principles perspective," Sharma said of Xbox's hopeful success. "And I think the industry will require disruption."
Sharma took over for former Xbox CEO Phil Spencer in February . Previously, she worked as Microsoft's CoreAI president. By July, Sharma's Xbox had laid off 1,600 people, with 1,600 more expected later this year. She described this move as "the most significant restructure in XBOX history" in a note to staff . Several studios have since closed , too. She claimed, in that note, that Xbox lost "64 cents for every dollar [Xbox] invested."
“We’ve got a long way to go with Microsoft, and we’re going to take the long-term view," Sharma told the New York Times.

title: Supercell, Rovio, Playdemic, First Touch, Sybo and more back SpecialEffect’s One Special Day
text:
Many major mobile game makers are giving a percentage of their UK revenue to disability charity Special Effect today, Friday October 2.
Partners taking part in the One Special Day promotion include Supercell, Rovio, Sybo, Playdemic, Fingersoft, Supersolid, Hyper Luminal Games, New Star Games, Miniclip, Green Man Gaming and MAG Interactive.
A slice of player spend from games including Clash of Clans, Brawl Stars, Clash Royale, Angry Birds 2, Golf Clash, Subway Surfers, Dream League Soccer, 8 Ball Pool and more will be donated to Special Effect for today only. A full list of participating games is available via the One Special Day site .
Special Effect provides assessments and customised technology loans to help physically disabled people play games, and takes what it learns back to hardware and software developers to help make their products more accessible. Thousands of disabled people ask for the charity’s help every year.
“We’ve been proud to partner with Special Effect across our games for nearly a decade, and that relationship has grown far beyond One Special Day,” said Supercell’s Deborah Mensah-Bonsu. “From cycling in Helsinki and joining One Special Walk in London, to learning from their incredible work as we think more deeply about inclusive design, we’re continually inspired by their tenacity, generosity and tremendous heart, and by how they show the games industry can genuinely change lives for the better.”
Special Effect COO Tom Donegan added: “We’re truly grateful to our partners for their generous involvement in One Special Day 2026. As demand for our projects and services continues to rise, this valuable contribution will play a vital role in helping us share the joy of gaming with thousands of people with physical disabilities around the world.”
This is the 11th edition of One Special Day, which this year has also included a Steam sale, a Green Man Gaming bundle beginning in early October, and the second One Special Walk in London, with the charity aiming to raise more than £500,000 across the campaign. Prior One Special Day events have included contributions from EA and First Touch Games in 2025, and Metacore in 2024.
Special Effect recently launched Open Drive , its first iOS game, designed for players with a wide range of physical disabilities.

title: New game digest: Sifu, Castlevania, Microsoft Jewel, One Piece, River City Survivors, more
text:
Here every Friday you’ll find the latest global releases, game dates, new soft launches and everything in between.
This column is sponsored by Kohort .
Ktrl is a data science muscle for your UA team without pulling anyone off product. See your own predictions free .
Sifu (Sloclap)
Sloclap is bringing its acclaimed martial arts beat ’em up Sifu to iOS and Android on October 12 for $7.99. The mobile port has touch-first controls and a contextual combat system built to preserve the original’s combos and parries on a smaller screen. Pre-orders are open now on the App Store and Google Play.
Castlevania (Konami)
Konami is marking Castlevania’s 40th anniversary by making the original 1986 game free on the App Store and Google Play. It’s available for no charge between now and October 24.
Microsoft Jewel (Microsoft Casual Games)
As spotted by The Verge , this casual puzzler has come to iOS and Android shortly after King took Microsoft Casual Games under its wing as part of the ongoing Xbox reorganisation. Microsoft Jewel apparently includes Xbox achievements, and signing into the game with your Microsoft account allows syncing across iOS, Android and PC.
One Piece: Grand Gourmet (Bandai Namco)
Bandai Namco’s One Piece: Grand Gourmet is a restaurant management sim built around the Straw Hat Crew that’s open for pre-registration. It launches on October 23.
River City Survivors: Downtown of the Dead (Arc System Works)
Arc System Works’ retro brawling series goes horde-survivor this week with River City Survivors: Downtown of the Dead, launching exclusively on Apple Arcade with over 20 unlockable characters, including series mainstays Kunio and Riki.
Namco Legendary Mountains (BeXide/Bandai Namco)
As spotted by Time Extension , BeXide’s voxel puzzler Namco Legendary Mountains is out now on iOS and Android. It’s a physics stacker built around merging capsules containing voxel versions of classic Namco arcade characters, having already released on PC and Switch in June.
New Three Kingdoms: Glory Reborn (Tencent)
Tencent is soft launching a new Three Kingdoms strategy title in China. It’s currently in pre-order, but only a Simplified Chinese build is available.
Codenames Party on Netflix Games (Czech Games Edition)
Czech Games Edition’s Codenames Party has landed on Netflix Games, playable on smart TVs and browsers with phones as controllers. It’s included with any Netflix membership.
Lil’ Guardsman (Plug In Digital)
After its run on Steam, tinyBuild’s narrative adventure Lil’ Guardsman heads to iOS and Android on November 10, published by Plug In Digital.
State of Desire (FunPlus)
Prison management meets gang politics in State of Desire, which Chan Gaming and FunPlus International released September 22 as a free 18+ app. It looks like it’s been soft launched in the US and Indonesia so far.
Dragon Village 3 (Highbrow)
Highbrow’s creature collecting series continues with Dragon Village 3, free now on the App Store and Google Play with village building, PvP, Raids and World Boss battles added to the mix.
The House of Tesla: Definitive Edition (Blue Brain Games)
The House of Da Vinci developer Blue Brain Games has its puzzle adventure follow-up, The House of Tesla: Definitive Edition, up for pre-order on iOS now, priced $6.99 / €6.99 / £6.99 ahead of an October 20 release on iOS and Android.
Titan Saga: Idle (Kneeshaw Developments)
Kneeshaw Developments has put out Titan Saga: Idle , a free faction management idle game for iOS and Android built to live-test systems for its upcoming open world sim, Titan Saga.

title: 战马工作室成立15年，创始人从来不走寻常路
text:
马丁·克里玛（Martin Klíma）喜欢挑战成规。在捷克战马工作室，这位联合创始人带领团队不走寻常路，开发了过去10年间最硬核、最独特，同时也最出色的角色扮演游戏之一——《天国：拯救2》。鲜为人知的是，他还曾是捷克斯洛伐克的一名学生运动成员。
马丁·克里玛曾是捷克斯洛伐克的一名学生运动分子
前不久，克里玛和同事们一起庆祝了战马成立15周年。在克里玛充满传奇色彩的人生中，这无疑是个里程碑式的时刻。“如今回想起来，我感觉那就像昨天才发生的事情。”2011年7月，克里玛和另一名性格桀骜不驯的开发者丹尼尔·瓦夫拉（Daniel Vávra）在离开大厂后自立门户，共同创办了战马工作室。不过，克里玛的职业生涯并非始于战马的创立，而是要追溯到上世纪80年代，捷克斯洛伐克解体之前。
■ 回忆往事
“我想在学校学英语，但这事儿挺难。”57岁的克里玛回忆。上世纪80年代，捷克斯洛伐克只能从友好国家进口英语教材，而加纳是它唯一以英语为官方语言的友好国家。克里玛承认，他对加纳英语教材里的内容完全不感兴趣。“我无意冒犯加纳人民，可我确实觉得，加纳教材教孩子们学习英语的方式相当另类：课本里的词汇以联合收割机、高炉这类事物为主，很少涉及孩子们更感兴趣的宝剑或矮人。”
在青少年时期，克里玛特别想读一读长篇奇幻小说《指环王》——当时，这部著作尚未在捷克斯洛伐克正式出版。直到1987年前后，克里玛终于托朋友从国外带回了一本《指环王》。“然而，那时候我英语水平有待提升，无法阅读原著……现在我之所以能够流畅自如地用英语接受采访，还得归功于J.R.R.托尔金。”
不久后，克里玛又幸运地得到了从国外进口的另一件奇幻珍品：《龙与地下城基础套装》。“与许多其他玩家一样，我在初次游玩《龙与地下城》时获得了妙不可言的体验。”他说，“我惊讶地发现，我可以扮演某个角色，并在奇幻世界里亲历那些精彩绝伦的冒险。”
《龙与地下城》激发了克里玛的热情，他决定将这款桌游翻译成本国语言，让更多同胞感受其独特魅力。“我和女友一起动手，完成了大约80%文本的翻译。”克里玛打算通过捷克斯洛伐克的地下印刷渠道出版《龙与地下城》译本，“至于正式翻译，获得官方授权……我们连想都不敢想。”有趣的是，在那之前，克里玛已经积累了实操经验：他曾负责出版一本校园科幻杂志，通过“将文章伪装成学生投稿”，悄悄发表热门科幻小说。
然而，由于生活中还有更重要的事情要做，克里玛不得不暂时搁置秘密传播《龙与地下城》的梦想。作为布拉格大学的学生，克里玛曾经成功组织了一次反对拆除校园内建筑的请愿活动。按照克里玛的说法，在上世纪80年代前的几十年里，捷克斯洛伐克民众或许会对他发起的请愿活动避之不及，但到80年代末，情况已经发生巨变。
■ 掷骰博弈
上世纪90年代初，捷克斯洛伐克发生巨大变化，并且在1993年变成捷克和斯洛伐克两个国家，克里玛开始尝试在游戏行业施展拳脚。当捷克国内局势平稳后，他和女友重新拾起了《龙与地下城》的翻译工作。“我给《龙与地下城》的发行商威世智写过信，对方没搭理。我甚至拜托在美国的亲戚帮忙写信、发传真，却从未收到任何回复。”克里玛透露，“威世智也许觉得我的想法太疯狂：‘那里的一群年轻人，怎么会想玩《龙与地下城》呢？在威世智看来，这可能太荒谬了。’”
受德国桌面角色扮演游戏《黑睛》（Das Schwarze Auge）启发，克里玛决定在他和女友已经完成的工作成果的基础上，创作一部全新作品。“我们重写大部分文本，设计专属职业和种族，还自创了一套战斗系统。”他说，“我们之所以要发明新的战斗系统，部分原因是在那个年代，捷克斯洛伐克没有生产20面骰子的条件，市面上只有6面和10面骰子。”
经过一段时间的努力，克里玛和女友拿出了一款玩法与《龙与地下城》高度相似的桌游：《龙穴》（Dračí doupě）。“《龙穴》取得了巨大成功，因为它是捷克斯洛伐克首款奇幻角色扮演桌游，就像在久旱成灾的沙漠，一场新雨后破土而出的绿芽……自那以后，我从未离开游戏行业。”
在职业生涯中，克里玛曾经为《龙穴》发行商Altar Publishing旗下公司Altar Interactive工作多年，参与开发了《Fish Fillets》、《原始战争》（Original War）和《UFO：余波》（UFO: Aftermath）等电脑游戏。2011年创办战马工作室前，克里玛丰富的从业履历足以写成一本书，不过他承认，他在与发行商打交道时屡屡受挫，对发行商的不满情绪越积越深。
《Vision》游戏画面
“本世纪头10年的末期，捷克桌游和电子游戏设计师弗拉达·赫瓦季尔（Vlaada Chvátil）领衔开发了一款被称为《Vision》的角色扮演游戏，发行商是德国公司CDV Software。当时我就想，这款游戏注定会创造历史，推动公司迎来重大突破。”克里玛回忆。
然而，发行商的态度却没那么乐观。“CDV先是要求我们对游戏做一些改动，后来又告诉我们，当初代表公司与我们签约的那位总经理已经离职，他们对改动后的游戏不再感兴趣。大约6个月后，CDV也破产了。我们有些心灰意冷，将公司卖给了波西米亚互动（Bohemia Interactive）。”
2010年9月，波西米亚互动正式完成对Altar Interactive的收购。克里玛在那里待了一段时间，随后短暂供职于Codemasters，不过很快就经过《闪点行动》首席设计师维克多·博坎（Viktor Bocan，现担任战马联席创意总监）牵线搭桥，与丹尼尔·瓦夫拉建立了联系。克里玛透露：“维克多告诉我，丹尼尔计划打造一款以15世纪的波西米亚王国为背景、高度写实的RPG游戏，正在寻找一位擅长使用Excel，愿意处理那些与数据、计划等相关的枯燥事务的伙伴。”经过沟通，克里玛和瓦夫拉一拍即合，战马工作室就这样诞生了。
■ 另辟蹊径
一个有趣的问题是，如果克里玛能够穿越时光回到过去，告诉多年前的自己，《天国：拯救》将会取得怎样的成绩，他是否会感到惊讶？克里玛对此表示，初代《天国：拯救》的成功并不出乎他的意料。不过他承认，考虑到战马曾经遭遇的重重困难和挑战，他一度担心工作室无法完成这款游戏的制作。
“当时我们需要一大笔钱。”克里玛回忆，“我们想要开发一款以高度写实、硬核还原为特色，甚至对玩家穿戴盔甲的顺序都极其考究的历史题材角色扮演游戏，但绝大多数发行商不敢冒险支持像这样的项目。那些日子太难熬了，我们花了整整两年时间才找到一位投资人。”
克里玛提到的投资者是美国捷克裔亿万富翁、风险投资家兹德涅克·巴卡拉（Zdeněk Bakala），此人提供的资金让他和几位合伙人得以扩大团队规模，着手开发《天国：拯救》，却并不足以支撑战马完成整款游戏的制作。“我们为《天国：拯救》构建了一个相当不错的垂直切片原型，委托代理机构宣传，奔波于世界各地，与三大洲大约50家不同发行商进行洽谈。然而，没有任何一家发行商对《天国：拯救》感兴趣。”
《天国：拯救》最初很难找到投资
与主流发行商相比，游戏玩家似乎更愿意支持这款风格独特的中世纪RPG。在Kickstarter平台，战马为《天国：拯救》发起众筹活动，并吸引了超过3.5万人参与。“许多玩家之所以参与《天国：拯救》的众筹，关键在于它能够满足玩家对更成熟、更具深度的角色扮演体验的追求。”克里玛指出，“相比之下，那些让玩家扮演‘天选之子’的RPG实在令人厌倦……当时，没有任何其他工作室制作类似的游戏：‘这是一款大型RPG，但你只是个无名小卒，注定无法成为拯救世界的英雄。’”
“发行商往往非常保守，因为随着游戏开发成本不断上涨，动辄达到上亿美元，他们必须卖出400万～500万份才能勉强回本。对于一款采用全新IP的游戏来说，这绝非易事。我在游戏行业已经摸爬滚打30年，迄今为止只成功说服发行商签下了一款游戏，那就是1997年发售的《原始战争》。如今回想起来，向发行商推销《天国：拯救》的经历让我大开眼界，深刻体会到这就像一项几乎不可能完成的任务。因此，当我们看到《天国：拯救》的理念获得玩家广泛认可时，那种如释重负的感觉真是太棒了。”
■ 未来征途
按照克里玛的说法，初代《天国：拯救》并没有实现战马工作室的宏大愿景，“它更接近《天国：拯救》的0.8版本”。不过，这款角色扮演游戏足以让战马扩大团队规模，并踏上开发续作的征程。
“有人说《天国：拯救》比续作更出色，声称《天国：拯救2》只是一款面向大众、玩法简化，甚至可以无脑游玩的平庸之作。我不同意这个观点，但我能理解为什么某些玩家会这么想。话说回来，《天国：拯救》每隔3小时就崩溃一次的体验确实太糟糕啦。”克里玛打趣，“哪怕你是最硬核的玩家，也会觉得难以忍受。”
对克里玛来说，《天国：拯救2》帮助他完成了一次奇妙的循环：年轻时他曾靠阅读《指环王》原著自学英语，如今则亲自与版权方洽谈，为战马工作室拿下了“指环王”IP衍生游戏的开发权。“很显然，正是因为《天国：拯救2》获得了成功，版权方才愿意为我们提供IP授权，放心地让我们为《指环王》制作游戏。”
战马工作室拿下了“指环王”IP衍生游戏的开发权
除了“指环王”IP衍生游戏之外，战马还在为“天国：拯救”系列开发一部新作。据克里玛透露，与过去相比，战马对工作室的组织结构做出了调整。“我们的开发人员已经共事多年，曾长期属于同一支团队，直到现在仍然坐在同一间办公室里。然而，为了推进两个不同项目，我们不得不将他们拆分成两支团队。”
克里玛聊了聊他对游戏行业当前所处困境的看法。在他看来，游戏市场的增长很可能已经触顶，未来继续增长的空间十分有限。“当厂商组建团队开发新游戏时，投入更多人手意味着项目成本上升，而这又意味着厂商必须卖出更多份游戏才不会亏本。”克里玛指出，“我们该怎么做呢？最简单的做法是进一步扩大市场，但整个市场早已触及天花板。我们无法让那些不想玩游戏，或者没钱玩游戏的人变成玩家。市场盘子就这么大，我们改变不了，除非我们能教会小狗玩游戏。”
“为了从现有玩家群体手中赚更多钱，我们可以把中间商踢出局，但我们早就这么干过，效果却很有限：我们摧毁了零售渠道，把他们的钱全赚走了。”克里玛半开玩笑地说，“无论如何，厂商绝对不敢轻率地提高游戏售价，大家都怕得要死……但愿《GTA6》能开先河吧！”
《GTA6》能否带动其他厂商提高游戏定价？这是个问题
与此同时，随着技术不断进步，玩家对游戏的期望值也越来越高了。“我的看法是，游戏厂商只能将开发工作转移到人力成本更低的国家和地区，比如中欧、东欧、印度，或者泛东亚地区，除此之外别无选择。我并不喜欢散布悲观言论，但我认为在北美和西欧，游戏行业当下的问题确实极其严重。”
许多游戏公司的高管热衷于利用AI工具来降本增效，但克里玛指出，对于如何在工作流程中引入AI，高管们的思维方式往往过于简单，在现实中并不可行。
“某些高管想当然地认为，既然AI能带来5倍的效能提升，他们完全可以将一支200人团队缩减到只剩下40人。按照他们的想法，就算每名开发者都需要配备专属AI，并且每个AI的成本与开发者大致相当，公司也只需要付出相当于一支80人团队的成本，就能完成一支200人团队的工作量。”克里玛解释。
“然而，即便不考虑AI生成内容的质量问题，现实情况也没这么简单。假设你有200名开发人员，以及某种能够让开发者的产出增加5倍的神奇AI，那么玩家对游戏品质的要求将会大幅上升，希望它能够对标1000人团队的作品。AI不是挡箭牌，它无法降低游戏制作成本，但能够让我们以同样的成本，打造出规模更大的游戏。”
本文编译自： pcgamer

title: Gears Of War: E-Day Has A Clever Solution To One Of PC Gaming’s Biggest Annoyances
text:
Early access for Gears of War: E-Day has kicked off for anyone who bought the Premium Edition, and if you're on PC, you're probably dreading the traditional shader compilation wait that comes with it. There's good news, as Gears of War: E-Day supports a neat feature on this platform that cuts down on that process significantly.
Called Advanced Shader Delivery (ASD), it addresses how modern games rely on shaders to calculate how light, shadows, reflections, and textures should look on screen. This usually involves you sitting for a while when you first boot up a game after installing it, resulting in the infamous "Compiling Shaders" loading bar. In comparison, ASD is like buying a Gundam model kit that's already assembled, right out of the box.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xTxwN-Ck1Zw
ASD pre-translates and delivers shader files directly to your device ahead of time, so you wait mere seconds. It also works across a wide variety of systems, and while I haven't installed Gears of War: E-Day on my main PC yet, I did load it up on my Asus Xbox ROG Ally X. The shader compilation waiting time was around 20 seconds, far better than waiting up to 15 minutes as I've experienced with other new games.
It's also worth noting that ASD works with multiple hardware configurations, including devices powered by AMD, Intel, Nvidia, and Qualcomm. Gears of War: E-Day will be the first game to support ASD across Windows devices, and it's currently available for users with AMD graphics cards. Owners of Nvidia GPUs will receive ASD-compatible drivers shortly after E-Day launches.
I was slaying the Locust, not my patience.
While our impression of the multiplayer portion of Gears of War: E-Day is still coming, the campaign is a mostly solid excuse to take cover and pop some Locust heads. "For better or worse, E-Day is distinctly Gears, and I had a good time with it, even if the story is disappointing and the open areas are fairly dull," Richard Wakeling wrote in GameSpot's Gears of War: E-Day review . "But that’s all it is: a good game, propped up by combat that hasn’t changed all that much over the past 20 years. That’s enough to skate by, but I wish Gears of War would dig deeper."

title: The Xbox Cloud Gaming Controller Is Not Dead, Apparently
text:
Microsoft agreed to several big changes to appease regulators in its effort to get the blockbuster $75.4 billion deal to buy Activision Blizzard approved, including tweaks to its cloud-gaming projects. Now, more than a year later, we're still learning more about this, including a new claim from The New York Times that Microsoft canceled plans for a new Xbox controller "devoted to cloud gaming."
A spokesperson for Microsoft denied that the controller concept was abandoned due to the regulatory process. Separately, sources told Windows Central that "rumors that Microsoft has canceled upcoming Xbox Cloud Gaming controllers are false."
Microsoft never formally announced or unveiled any controller for cloud gaming, but an image of it leaked this year, prompting raised eyebrows for its ... unique design.
Microsoft cut deals with a variety of companies--including Ubisoft , Nware , EE, Boosteroid , Ubitus , and Nvidia --to help mitigate concerns from the UK's Competition & Markets Authority (CMA) that Microsoft might give preferential treatment to its own cloud gaming networks.
Former Xbox CEO Phil Spencer, who led Xbox during the sale process, said such deals freed up one of the concerns the CMA had and helped bring more games to more people.
The Xbox cloud-gaming service showed some initial signs of growth , but the program suffered a setback recently when Microsoft announced that it will soon put limits on how much people can use the service , and then charge them more to keep playing. Additionally, Windows Central recently discovered that the dedicated cloud gaming app for older Samsung TVs will go away soon due to a compatibility issue. The site later reported that the support for older Samsung TVs is due to "the lack of updates those sets are getting" as Samsung focuses on its newer units.
Additionally, sources told Windows Central "there are absolutely no plans to decelerate on Xbox Cloud Gaming" generally.
Access to cloud gaming is one of the perks of Xbox Game Pass Ultimate, allowing people to stream their games. Later this year, people will be able to buy game time for cloud gaming on Xbox without a Game Pass membership.
One of the appeals of cloud gaming, at least in theory, is that it requires no expensive local hardware like an Xbox or PC, both of which are more expensive than ever due to the AI-fueled demand for memory and components. People need a consistent and fast internet connection for the best experience.
In other Xbox news, CEO Asha Sharma recently stressed that Xbox is "not for sale," following rumors and reports that Microsoft could unload the struggling company.

title: PS5 Just Got A PS5 Pro-Like AI Upgrade, But Don’t Expect It Everywhere Yet
text:
The base PS5 console is no slouch when it comes to games, but compared to the PS5 Pro, it doesn't pack the same visual punch. That could change soon, as Sony has unveiled a new AI-upscaling upgrade for the older machine called Spectral Super Resolution (QSSR). Like PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR), it is designed to make games look sharper and maximize performance.
While PSSR will still remain the "gold standard" for what Sony games can look like on PS5 Pro, QSSR looks like it'll offer a noticeable improvement on PS5. A result of the AI graphics collaboration with AMD, Sony says that it offers a "streamlined neural network architecture" for games. The only catch? For now, only two PS5 games will support it: Marvel's Wolverine and Ghost of Yotei --which is getting a new Complete Edition this month. Here are a few samples of it in action:
https://youtu.be/RcFYsDKbAIk
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=E929-XwrS_Q
"QSSR adds more pixel-level clarity and stability to our environments, bringing out extra detail amidst the busy streets of Madripoor, the dense alleyways of Shinjuku, and many other areas across Logan's epic journey. It’s a perfect companion to the launch of Marvel's Wolverine, and it brings a great taste of the PS5 Pro experience to our players on PS5," head of technology at Insomniac Games, Mike Fitzgerald, wrote in a PS Blog post .
Jasmin Patry, lead rendering engineer at Ghost of Yotei developer Sucker Punch Productions, added that QSSR excels at "resolving the fine details" in characters and environments that previously wasn't possible on the base PS5. Both PS5 exclusives are receiving a patch today to add QSSR as an additional graphics option, and Sony says it will be offered to all PlayStation developers soon.
If it's implemented widely and across many more games, QSSR could become a big selling point for the PS5, as the console will be six years old in November. Price hikes have made it more expensive to jump into the current console generation, and for anyone who can afford the $900 PS5 Pro , stock seems increasingly harder to find as demand begins to outpace supply. In Japan, potential consumers are now being asked to enter a lottery system and prove they've played at least 60 hours over the last two years on their current PS5 console.
In comparison, an improved gaming experience on a regular PS5 console sounds like it makes financial sense--even if the console was much cheaper when it first launched in 2020.

title: Blizzard Isn’t Fixing Diablo 4 Season 15’s Biggest Bug
text:
Diablo 4 Season 15's biggest bug, one revolving around Hellfire Torch and being able to equip more Unique charms than should be possible, won't be fixed this season, Blizzard has announced.
Hellfire Torch is a new Unique charm that counts as an extra set charm and comes with some great beneficial stats, like +All Skills, +All Stats, and +All Resistances. Players can usually only have one Unique charm equipped at a time, but Hellfire Torch breaks that rule, allowing players to use it and another Unique charm.
That's strong on its own, but there is currently a bugged interaction with Hellfire Torch that is allowing players to equip two Unique charms in addition to Hellfire Torch instead of one, granting even higher levels of power.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2L55dgNzpQ8
The bug seems to stem from Hellfire Torch being used first alongside the Seal of the Golden Epiphany, which allows players to equip up to three Unique charms. However, players are later swapping out Golden Epiphany for the Mythic Seal of the Diamond Mind, a seal that reduces the number of charms needed for set bonuses, but are still able to benefit from having additional Unique charms equipped. That, in turn, allows players to gain advantages from a full five-piece set bonus, Hellfire Torch, and two Unique charms all at once.
Now, Diablo 4 design director Dan Tanguay in a forum post said Blizzard is aware of the bug and said Hellfire Torch' s current behavior is "beyond what was originally intended." That being said, Blizzard will be letting it ride this season as it works towards a fix in the future.
"We know many players have spent significant time earning the Hellfire Torch and building characters around it," Tanguay said. "Because of that, we want to be thoughtful about making adjustments mid-season that could disrupt those investments."
Tanguay continued: "We've also seen the positive reception to the Hellfire Torch itself from many players. The item has created a lot of excitement this season, and we've taken note of the feedback from those who have enjoyed earning it and incorporating it into their builds. While we don't have anything to announce today, it is something we're considering for the future, which makes it even more important that we fully understand and address this interaction the right way."
The post states Blizzard will continue to investigate the issue so that any future changes will be "implemented correctly and behave as intended."
Players in Season 15 just might be stronger than ever before. Alongside the bugged Hellfire Torch interaction, players can also use this trick to get around the game's crafted Mythic item restriction and fully deck themselves out in Mythic gear.
It's just the last development in what has been one of Diablo 4's wildest, and most surprising, seasons yet. Season 15, Hell's Legacy, introduced all kinds of new content based on previous Diablo games, including boss fights against Diablo, Baal, and Mephisto ripped straight from earlier entries in the franchise. It's also filled to the brim with secrets upon secrets , including a showdown with the cow god Moophisto and even the return of the secret pony level, Whimsyshire, from Diablo 3.
Diablo 4 will continue to receive new seasons going forward, but won't be getting new expansions , as Blizzard instead shifts its focus to Diablo 5 . A new Diablo 4 class , the Amazon, will release as standalone DLC in the first half of 2027.

title: GTA 6’s Weather System Sounds Like A Big Step Up
text:
Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 includes a number of updates and improvements over the developer's past games, and that includes new weather systems.
Rockstar's vice president of art for lighting and rendering at Rockstar, Owen Shepherd, told Game Informer that the studio has "re-engineered" the studio's weather system to "make everything more more localized and persistent."
He said the goal was to make the weather in GTA 6's setting of Leonida--a stand-in for Florida--feel "dynamically solid and achieve a sense of scale" that the studio has never done before.
GTA 6 launches on November 19.
What that means in practice is that GTA 6 will have "fully dynamic cloudscapes that roll across the map" to provide a "broad spectrum of weather" in the game.
Florida is known for its heat and humidity, along with its localized and fast-moving rain systems. Look one direction and you may see bright sunshine. Look the other and you could see a downpour. GTA 6 will replicate this with localized rain showers, along with rainbows that appear. Additionally, places where it recently rained in the game will remain wet, with puddles also popping up.
GTA 6 also has a new wind system that includes "offshore breezes after sunset, convectional updrafts, and occlusion from buildings,” Shepherd said. “Hair and debris will swirl around on rooftops; gusts of wind will blow ripples over the water surface and bend the grass in swamps.”
GTA 6 will also include tropical storms and hurricanes, along with thunder and lightning. Shepherd did not, however, get into how GTA 6's new weather systems could affect gameplay. Florida is known to experience devastating hurricanes, but it remains to be seen if, for example, a hurricane could knock down structures or trees.
GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, priced at $80 for its standard edition and $100 for the Ultimate Edition. Rockstar is also selling a $400 collector's edition that includes a bunch of physical goodies, but not the game.

title: PS5’s Exciting New Zelda-Like Kena Game Just Got Delayed
text:
Developer Ember Lab has announced that its upcoming PS5 game Kena: Scars of Kosmora, the sequel to 2021's much-loved Kena: Bridge of Spirits, has been delayed. The game-- which gives off major Zelda vibes --was previously set to release this year , but now it's been delayed to 2027.
In a blog post , the developers said they need more time to "deliver a top-notch game that exceeds the quality" of Bridge of Spirits. "Pushing our release into 2027 gives us the ability to really polish the expanded game experience we want to deliver," the studio said.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BhgxkBxiCyg
Scars of Kosmora is a linear adventure game, just like the 2021 entry, but the sequel has a "broader and deeper scope," the studio said.
"We hope you’re just as excited to jump into Kena’s next adventure as we are to share it with you. We’ve been working hard to fill it with the wonder, charm, and challenge fans have come to expect," the team added. "We appreciate your patience and support as we take the time for Scars of Kosmora to be the evolution of Kena’s journey and experience we want to deliver."
In Scars of Kosmora, main character Kena is now a seasoned spirit guide and embarks on a journey to the island of Kosmora to find a "cure for her affliction and to reconnect with a friend from her past." The island holds a "powerful corruption" that fractures her staff, so Kena adopts a new method of manipulating the elements to her advantage.
"On her journey, Kena discovers and nurtures memorable spirit companions-- whose powers she will harness to solve puzzles and defeat enemies using new elemental abilities," reads a line from the game's description.
2021's Bridge of Spirits was released initially on PS4, PS5, and PC, and later came to Xbox One and Xbox Series X|S in 2024. A Switch 2 edition arrived in March this year. Kosmora has been confirmed only for PS5 and PC so far.

title: Activision Could Be Giving Halo Something It Hasn’t Had In Years: A Clean Slate
text:
Halo has a new home at Activision following recent changes at Xbox , and while it's still early days, Activision has reportedly proposed a total reboot for the series. This would be a fresh start, moving away from the convoluted Halo lore built up over the last 25 years through various games and spin-off media. That's according to sources who spoke to Rebs Gaming, who also stressed that nothing is concrete right now. Call of Duty developer Sledgehammer Games presented conceptual prototypes for a free-to-play multiplayer game and a story campaign built in the Infinity Ward engine, and it's believed the studio will lead development.
"Activision is building a development team for the next Halo game, and based on my information, that team could be built within Sledgehammer Games. I'm also told they created the prototypes in the Infinity Ward engine. This doesn't confirm the game will be developed in Call of Duty's engine instead of Unreal Engine, but the prototypes indicate it's definitely possible. Apparently, Activision's idea for the campaign project was a soft reboot that doesn't follow Halo Infinite's story, but also doesn't retcon established canon," Rebs Gaming said.
"However, it sounds like plans are changing. I'm told they discarded their original project ideas for a full Halo game."
https://youtu.be/wPWqTRrCgX0
Rebs Gaming added that this means a sequel to Halo Infinite is unlikely and that "at least some of Halo's story" will be rebooted. One major criticism of Halo after its original developer, Bungie, left the franchise and handed it over to 343 Industries/Halo Studios was that the franchise shifted away from telling standalone stories. Halo books and media were supplementary material that added to the franchise, but weren't essential to the overall narrative.
But with Halo Studios, there was a period of mandatory homework for fans as novels, comics, and spin-off games featured crucial plot points and new characters. For example, the Forerunner history in Halo 4 and the appearance of Blue Team in Halo 5 required outside reading to understand what was going on, while later games jettisoned major villains like the Didact and Jul 'Mdama, resulting in a messy lore with abrupt resets.
In related Halo news, former franchise director Frank O’Connor offered plenty of advice to Activision as it builds the new game, including pitfalls it should avoid.

title: The Street Fighter Movie’s Most Obscure Easter Egg Is For True Fighting Game Nerds
text:
Ahead of its release later this month, marketing for the Street Fighter movie has focused on deep references to the long-running fighting game series. How deep? We already knew that fighting game legend Justin Wong--alongside Michael "IFC Yipes" Mendoza--was making a cameo as one of the inmates who watches Ryu take on Blanka in a prison fight , but even his prisoner costume hides one heck of an Easter egg. Any fighting game fan will instantly recognize it: on Wong's neck, you can spot the number 37, a reference to the legendary Evo Moment 37 .
In a new behind-the-scenes video, Wong detailed the time he spent on the Street Fighter movie set getting fake dirt and dressing up for his cameo. If you're unfamiliar with the significance of the fake 37 tattoo his character sports, it's a deep-cut nod to what many consider one of the greatest fighting game comebacks in history. Back in 2004, Wong faced off against Daigo Umehara, and with his chosen brawler, Chun-Li, down to just a sliver of health and backed into a corner, Wong parried over a dozen attacks from Umehara's Ken Masters and found the perfect window to counter the onslaught.
https://youtu.be/ssipFrggf58
It's a moment that has yet to be equaled within the fighting game community, with the clip earning an obscene number of views over the decades. This is just the tip of the iceberg when it comes to the accuracy the Street Fighter movie is aiming for, as the film embraces the unique look of the Capcom games with its choice of costumes, special attacks, and goofy hairstyles that double as the perfect popcorn bucket . Chun-Li actress Callina Liang even went the extra mile to get into fighting shape for the movie, focusing on conditioning her thighs to look impressively muscular and memorizing Chun-Li's various attacks.
On the audio side, composers Leo Birenberg and Zach Robinson (Cobra Kai) have even used classic video game soundtracks for the film's score, including a new version of Guile's theme that fits everything . Street Fighter hits theaters on October 16.
