title: Disney Responds To Rumor That It Could Buy Fortnite Studio Epic Games
text:
One juicy gaming rumor that continues to swirl is that The Walt Disney Company could buy Epic Games and Fortnite. It remains to be seen if such a deal may materialize, and now a top boss at the House of Mouse has directly responded.
Speaking at Bloomberg's Screentime event this week, Disney executive Dana Walden reminded everyone that Disney already i nvested more than $1.5 billion into Epic for an equity stake . But could talks progress to a full acquisition?
"Those are not the conversations we're having right now," Walden said. "But we have a great partnership."
Disney and Epic are working together to create “transformational” new games . So far, they have showed up in Fortnite in a variety of ways, including the recent integration of Fortnite at Disney's real-world parks .
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Yf2bRcSIUsE
Walden said people can look forward to even more to come in the next few years. "A number of launches coming up over the next two years ... are going to demonstrate the value of this partnership," she said.
Kevin Mayer–a former Disney and TikTok executive who now runs Candle Media–said Disney's new CEO, Josh D’Amaro, will need to take “bold steps” to help Disney make more money and grow its stock price. One part of this could be buying Epic Games or another game studio , he said.
Technology reporter Alex Heath recently said on Matthew Belloni’s podcast, The Town , that he knows “for a fact” that some senior executives at Disney want to buy Epic Games and are waiting for the right moment. Other executives at Disney believe it would be a bad idea, Heath said.
Epic Games is a founder-controlled company, with CEO Tim Sweeney retaining full voting stock control. He has the ability to make unilateral decisions to control and secure Epic's future.
Epic would not be Disney’s first potential acquisition target. In 2023, it was reported that Disney was interested in pursuing a purchase of Electronic Arts , but nothing ever came of that, and now EA has been sold to Saudi Arabia's PIF.
Beyond Disney's investment in Epic for Fortnite, some of Disney's shows, like The Mandalorian, use Epic’s Unreal Engine to project scenes onto LED screens surrounding the physical set.
D'Amaro is a big believer in video games and has said he wants to do more in gaming going forward . Wall Street is looking for some kind of catalyst for Disney's stock, and many have said further investments into tech and gaming could be a way to help get Disney's stock price out of its 10-year slump. Disney stock exploded during COVID, but is actually lower today than it was a decade ago.
D'Amaro has floated numerous ideas for further Disney integration into Fortnite, including giving players the ability to book Disney cruises or watch a Disney movie on the platform .
Fortnite is a big push from Disney in gaming, but it's just one small piece. Disney today has nine gaming franchises that have individually earned more than $1 billion .

title: Blizzard Might Finally Be Serious About WoW: Forever Gold Buying, Bans Streamer For Promoting It
text:
A prominent World of Warcraft: Forever streamer has been banned following comments made on stream encouraging his viewers to buy gold on his behalf.
Forever, which is currently in beta ahead of the MMORPG's full launch in November, is currently mired in a gold buying and real-money transaction (RMT) controversy. Players buying gold from third-party websites that use bots to farm the game's primary currency has been a problem for the entirety of WoW's existence and has always been against the game's terms of service. What's changed is that developer Blizzard has made comments that it's looking to more aggressively punish gold buyers in Forever, even going as far to admit its been too "lenient" on the matter in the past.
That more hardline stance against gold buyers was put to the test earlier this week when WoW: Forever streamer Ziqo was seen on stream accepting suspiciously large amounts of gold from strangers in the lead-up to a $100,000 prize pool PvP tournament he and many other streamers will be competing in. Given the huge sums of gold being traded, many believed there was little chance the gold had been acquired naturally through farming and was likely bought by a third party and then given to Ziqo as a gift.
https://youtu.be/dvueCoFTkCk?si=YqPAFYzvWt5J5WiC
Almost immediately, the Forever community was up in arms demanding Blizzard take action. In a forum post seemingly issued in response to the Ziqo controversy, Blizzard stated that it would increasingly punish not only gold sellers, its standard practice, but also those buying the gold. In addition, accounts accepting large amounts of questionable gold could also be punished by having the illicit gold removed, their account suspended, or even permanently banned. Blizzard encouraged players not to accept "suspicious" transactions to avoid these consequences.
Even if Ziqo wasn't the buyer, according to Blizzard's own words, he could in theory be punished for taking what many viewed to be ill-gained gold. That same gold in question was later removed from Ziqo's account by Blizzard, though the streamer was not banned or suspended, as many players called for.
https://www.reddit.com/r/classicwow/comments/1wtnmfr/i_never_hid_the_fact_that_i_wanted_my_chat_to_buy/?share_id=zh96vvQnxd9xojUBRfqN7&utm_content=share_button&utm_medium=web3x&utm_name=web3xcss&utm_source=share&utm_term=1
The same can't be said for another WoW streamer looking to participate in the game's upcoming tournament, Payo. Amidst the Ziqo drama, Payo said on stream he hadn't been shy about the fact he is more than okay with members of his community buying gold on his behalf.
"I never hid the fact I want my chat to use their credit cards to fill my bags," Payo said on stream.
Those comments look to have caught Blizzard's ire, as it was only a few days later that Payo's account had been banned from the game. He has since apologized and said he's never bought gold personally. He said he was "happy" about the ban, because it shows Blizzard is serious about the RMT problem.
Though his main account was banned, Payo was not banned permanently and was allowed to create another account and continue streaming Forever.
"I learned from my mistake, and I will never ever promote gold buying again, that's for sure," Payo said.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XKtc_UCcmZA
In the wake of Payo's ban, Blizzard issued another warning shot of a forum post . Community manager Kaivax in a post on October 1 said Blizzard has continued to take action against botting accounts and those who have bought or "knowingly received illicit gold." In addition, Kaivax announced Blizzard will be adding a warning to Forever that will appear when trading with strangers. The warning that will appear is as follows:
"Be wary of accepting gold from unknown or suspicious sources. If the provider is engaged in Real Money Transactions, you could put your account at risk of closure."
Kaivax concludes by making Blizzard's stance on RMT "crystal clear:"
"Any account belonging to any player that is found to have participated in generating, selling, buying, or receiving illicit gold is subject to the gold being removed, account suspensions, or permanent account closers."
Some players on places like the WoW Classic subreddit are still skeptical. Blizzard has always talked a big game about banning bots, for example, but as any WoW Classic player can tell you, botting is still a major issue. More than a few in the community point to the fact that Payo and Ziqo weren't permanently banned as Blizzard still being too lenient, especially towards streamers. For others, Blizzard going as far as adding an actual in-game warning about the dangerous consequences of engaging with RMT is a major escalation in the war against gold buyers and sellers.
"Players are being given plenty of warning," user Dessiato said in a post discussing Kaivax's forum post. "I look forward to the reckoning."
Whether Blizzard lives up to its word remains to be seen, but there's no doubt the Forever beta is putting WoW in the spotlight in a way that hasn't been seen since the launch of WoW Classic in 2019. Blizzard developers have commented that the Forever beta is breaking records , with the Forever beta population cap needing to be raised multiple times since its launch on September 17. The beta, which requires the purchase of the $60 Skyborne Heroic pack in order to gain access , will run until October 21. WoW: Forever launches in full November 4.

title: NBA’s Miami Heat Will Wear GTA 6 Jerseys And Play On A Branded Court The Day Before Release
text:

title: Sony’s Revised PS5 Slim Could Be Getting Cheaper To Make, But Not To Buy
text:
It looks like Sony has quietly revised the PS5 console once again, with new internal changes across the (mother)board. It's not clear when these new models came into service, but they seem to have entered circulation around the same time Sony released limited-edition Marvel's Wolverine PS5 consoles.
Spotted by Modyfikator89, longevity and repairability appear to be the key areas that Sony has focused on. The redesigned motherboard offers easier access to the CR2023 battery, the streamlined internal layout makes repairs less risky, and the hardware takes a page from the PS5 Pro playbook with refined liquid-metal containment and revised heatsink materials. In theory, the updated barrier around the processor die should keep the liquid metal better contained over time, ensuring stable thermal transfer performance even under intensive loads.
https://twitter.com/Modyfikator89/status/2105382987755814984
Sony has also moved to a newer, lower-cost HDMI retimer chip, which likely cuts down bill-of-materials costs and improves display signal stability. Overall, this will likely lower production costs while maintaining higher assembly yields, at a time when sourcing components has become more challenging. Companies routinely make stealth revisions to cut manufacturing costs, but unlike previous console generations that shrank and became cheaper over time, the PS5 has only gotten more expensive since it launched in November 2020.
When it first launched , the entry-level PS5 Digital Edition had an MSRP of $400, but in 2026, you can expect to pay $600 for one. The base model PS5 with a disc drive has increased from $500 to $650, while the PS5 Pro has shot up from $700 to $900. Sony is aiming to make the PS5 a better value proposition as it heads into the lucrative holiday season, after recently launching a new AI-upscaling technology for its base-model PS5s.
Only two of its exclusive games support it currently--Marvel's Wolverine and Ghost of Yotei--and the technology will be released to more developers soon. By enabling the base PS5 to deliver sharper visuals through Quick Spectral Super Resolution, Sony offers a visual upgrade in select games without having to splash out on the more expensive PS5 Pro.

title: In 5 Years, Will Netflix Still Be In Gaming? Here’s What The CEO Said
text:
Netflix has been experimenting with video games for a while, but is the streaming giant going to eventually drop out of gaming? That's the question Bloomberg's Lucas Shaw put to Netflix co-CEO Ted Sarandos at the Screentime event this week .
Regarding whether Netflix will still host games in five years, Sarandos said, "I think so." He said Netflix's push into mobile gaming was "a gateway to cloud gaming," which is something Netflix is "much more interested in."
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1lsV9I2NDO8
Netflix hosts a variety of mobile games, including Red Dead Redemption, Sonic Mania Plus, and RollerCoaster Tycoon Touch, just to name a few. The games are included with a Netflix membership and have no ads. Netflix also hosts streaming games that can be played on your TV, and they are more family- and party-focused.
Netflix's gaming ambitions have bounced around over the years. At one point, the company wanted to make big, AAA games, and hired some big names to get it done. However, Netflix later wound down these efforts , closing studios and laying off staff in the process, leading many to wonder what Netflix's ambition for video games actually was.
Sarandos said cloud gaming makes more sense for Netflix "in a post-console world." He didn't elaborate here, but it sounds like he's talking about a future where more and more people play games without dedicated hardware like a PlayStation, Xbox, or Switch console. All of those systems have gone up in price in recent times due to AI-fueled component and memory issues, along with bigger global macroeconomic trends.
The cloud gaming market hasn't popped the way some have predicted, but Sarandos isn't the only person who is optimistic about the future potential. Strauss Zelnick, the head of GTA 6 owner Take-Two recently said , "I think we'll be in commercial streaming mode within three years."
Sarandos said there will be "all kinds of opportunities for gaming on the television," and the executive said Netflix wanted to be "early invested in that."
"I like it for IP extension. I certainly like it for brand value, for people who want to spend time on that screen gaming instead of watching, then we have an option for them," he said.
Also in the interview, Sarandos was asked if Netflix would again reach into its coffers to buy a large-scale gaming company to help its gaming ambitions become realized faster. The interviewer asked if Netflix could buy Take-Two or Xbox, and Sarandos said it doesn't have any specific plans to buy more gaming studios, though he's not ruling anything out either. For what it's worth, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma recently said Xbox is not for sale , while Take-Two selling itself would be shocking.
Sarandos said Netflix prefers to grow organically instead of buying companies to spur growth. Of course, this isn't a hard-and-fast rule, as evidenced by Netflix offering to buy Warner Bros. Discover for many billions of dollars before Paramount swooped in and made a deal. He said Netflix went after WBD because the company was "so clean" and contained only the elements and assets of the business that Netflix actually wanted, and that was rare.
Netflix will look at other opportunities to buy game studios if they complement the company's wider business goals, Sarandos said.
In other news about cloud gaming, Microsoft has reportedly canceled its new controller for it , ahead of price hikes to the service soon .
Netflix has also said it's still very early days for its gaming output, saying the company has “tons more work to do." Netflix's financial investment in gaming is minuscule relative to its other business areas, and management sees gaming as a "significant market opportunity." Netflix investors no doubt want to see Netflix find new ways to make money; after all, Netflix stock has crashed more than 25% in 2026 so far.

title: 索尼为标准版PS5带来AI超分功能「QSSR」
text:
首发登陆《漫威金刚狼》与《羊蹄山之魂》
AI超分辨率技术如今已成为现代图形处理流程的重要组成部分。虽然PSSR将这项技术带到了PS5 Pro，但由于GPU性能较弱，普通版PS5此前一直无法使用。如今，QSSR解决了这个问题。
索尼在一篇博客文章中详细介绍了这款可运行于普通版主机的新型超分辨率模型，其全称为（快速光谱超分辨率）Quick Spectral Super Resolution，简称QSSR。和今年早些时候在PS5 Pro上首次亮相的PSSR一样，QSSR也源自索尼与AMD展开的Project Amethyst合作项目，该项目于去年启动。
这款新模型比PSSR轻量得多，因此在保持细节方面不如PS5 Pro上的PSSR，但其准确度应该会明显高于主机传统使用的时间超分辨率技术。
QSSR将首次应用于《漫威金刚狼》和《羊蹄山之魂》，两款游戏的开发团队似乎都对将这项技术加入作品感到十分兴奋。索尼博客引用了Insomniac技术主管Mike Fitzgerald的话：「QSSR能为游戏环境带来更清晰的像素级画面和更稳定的表现，让马德里坡繁忙的街道、新宿错综复杂的小巷，以及罗根史诗旅程中的众多地点呈现更多细节。它是《漫威金刚狼》发售时的完美伴侣，也能让PS5玩家体验到PS5 Pro的一部分画面效果。」
同样，Sucker Punch首席渲染工程师Jasmin Patry表示：「Sucker Punch很高兴能将QSSR带给《羊蹄山之魂》玩家，让他们以更清晰、细致的画面体验我们创造的世界。QSSR尤其擅长还原角色和环境中的细微之处，并能提供迄今为止PS5主机尚未实现的时间稳定性。我们一直希望所有PS5玩家都能体验PSSR为PS5 Pro带来的惊艳画质，而QSSR正朝着这个目标迈出了积极一步！」
索尼还在博客中分享了两款游戏的演示片段，将启用QSSR的效果与普通版PS5上的标准时间超分辨率进行对比，结果相当令人期待。《漫威金刚狼》的片段放大了远处的建筑。虽然QSSR画面仍然比较模糊——毕竟这是一个削弱版模型——但与左侧的标准画面相比，它能在细小物体上保留更多细节。
随后，《羊蹄山之魂》的镜头放大了前景中的植被。在PS5原始画面中，草地几乎像是一堆漂浮的绿色线条，锯齿还将其切割成了不同部分。启用QSSR后，草地基本保持了真实形状，尽管画面仍然有些噪点。
显然，运行于性能更强的PS5 Pro上的模型，在保持画面质量方面肯定会优于QSSR。但PS5 Pro如今售价高达900美元，因此，这款更轻量的模型至少让更多人能够用上超分辨率技术。索尼表示，QSSR将向所有开发者开放，因此未来应该会有更多工作室采用这项技术。对于那些至少还要再过几个月才能负担得起、预计价格不菲的PS6（或者是PS5 Pro）的人来说，QSSR或许可以暂时缩小画质体验上的差距。

title: You can now play Halo: Combat Evolved in a web browser, and it even has multiplayer
text:
In an act that is both technically impressive and presumably legally dubious, a developer has got a build of the original Halo: Combat Evolved working in a web browser. And no, I didn't play the game instead of writing this article in a timely fashion; why do you ask?
Developer Mitchell Hynes recently took to X to share their browser-based rendition of Halo , and it works surprisingly well. Simply click on the site, wait for the browser to download anything it needs, and start playing. It even has full mouse and keyboard support.
It's all built off the decompilation project from Bnunu , who have been reverse-engineering the game for some time. It, combined with a fork from team Cybersecurity , supports 128-player multiplayer and works on Windows, Linux, and Android.
The site saw so much traffic from X that it very briefly went down, as it was automatically flagged for "suspected phishing", but has since come back online. Within just five hours, the browser-based project saw almost 20,000 games across 115 countries, according to the developer .
Notably, word of the site has since spread off X and has now made it to the Halo subreddit , where players are creating lobbies to battle it out.
IT'S HERE!!! HALO CE (XBOX) IN THE BROWSER!Features:✅ WORKING Splitscreen Co-op✅ WORKING Multiplayer up to 128 players (untested)❌ NO GEARBOX MASTER CHIEF pic.twitter.com/EgiHI6ji6l September 29, 2026
One Redditor says , "Lmao this is great. Got a couple good kills back and forth just using trackpad. I need to get back to work now but I'm excited for such a simple way to play with people."
The only issue with multiplayer is that there doesn't appear to be any matchmaking functionality. When you click on the multiplayer mode, it gives you a room link, which you can send to others to have them play with you. Servers are peer-to-peer, as you might expect, so make sure your host has a good connection.
In my experience, it works surprisingly well. It takes a while to load a mission, which I assume has something to do with my internet connection not being great today—but it's smooth to play, and the audio sounds great too.
My only concern is that this is a free way to play a classic game, and Microsoft just launched Halo: Campaign Evolved last month. I can't imagine MS likes the idea of players playing its games for free, and in a mere moment. Still, it's fun while it lasts.

title: Resident Evil's executive producer explains the deeper meaning behind Requiem, and I just can't get on board
text:
I was brought up with the mindset that when you start something you should see it through to the end, even if it gets a bit tricky. So perhaps that's why Resident Evil dropping its in-built Roman numerals irks me so.
It all started with Resident Evil: 7 Biohazard where the Roman numerals for seven were shoved into the 'E vil ' and then continued with Resident Evil: Vill age . So, in the lead up to Resident Evil 9 I was on tenterhooks, eager to find out how Capcom was going to incorporate IX into its title.
I had my own theories , settling on Helix or Appendix as my favourite options. It made sense in my head, what with their respective links to DNA as well as the T-virus, and an icky body part that simultaneously means something that comes at the end of a story—I really liked appendix.
Alas, we didn't get either or those—we didn't get an IX at all—we got Resident Evil Requiem .
(Image credit: K.C. Green) I made my peace with Requiem, it has cool connotations for the game, referring to a prayer for the soul of the deceased or a general act of remembering someone who has died. I also saw one promotional image that turned the 'q' in Requiem into the number nine, so that's something, maybe. But wait, there's more.
Resident Evil's executive producer Jun Takeuchi has revealed in chat with Japanese press for RE's 30th anniversary (via GamesRadar ) that the name Requiem holds much more than just the above, bog-standard meaning:
"Let me give you a hint: 'Requiem' isn't just a title chosen for its meaning of 'requiem.' The spelling of Requiem (REQUIEM) contains not only the 'RE (response)' mentioned earlier, but also a 'Q (question).' In other words, this 'Requiem' presents both an 'answer' and a 'question.' I will explain the meaning of that at some point in the future."
Yeah, I don't think I'm entirely on board with this breakdown of Requiem. I guess it makes sense but it's also giving off GCSE English blue curtain vibes. I am, however, intrigued to find out more about this in the future, and perhaps we can also discover what the rest of Requiem stands for. Who knows, it could go something like: 'U' for you the player, 'I' for me, the player, 'E' for evil residents, and 'M' for me, the player, again (I get two because I'm special).

title: After a series of catastrophes where no-one could seem to roll well, I truly have no idea who's going to make it out of Critical Role's next episode
text:
Critical Role's 4th's campaign is in full swing, and this past episode we followed the schemer's table—for those not in the know, this campaign's a "West Marches" style adventure, where the stacked cast of 13 players split off into their own groups.
The schemer's table, so named because of the political scheming it's involved in, just spent four and a half hours spinning out last week as the chickens came home to roost. Allow me to give you the bullet points (spoilers, obviously):
Halandil Fang's (played by Liam O'Brian) daughter has been expelled from school after the prior episode, where the equivalent of the pope personally popped in to threaten his life. He rolled a natural one to try and calm his now-revolutionary daughter down.
Azure Nayar (played by Luis Carazo) is getting pulled in all directions—playing nice with two sorcerous houses while being loyal to neither of them. Also, the head of one such house now thinks he's in a relationship with his cousin (he is not, he just has her axe, long story).
Murray Magnesson (played by Marisha Ray) is on the cusp of getting fired from her job at a school which is rapidly becoming less about teaching magic, and more raising soldiers for another sorcerous house while leaving them without any magic that'd be useful in standing up against them.
Also, Azure's boss hates her.
Tyranny, a demon (played by Whitney Moore), has been ordered by her father to destroy her corporeal form and return to hell.
Also, she got the crap kicked out of her by her sister (also a demon, also playing reformed bodyguard for the church, it's—don't worry about it).
Wicander Halovar (played by Sam Riegel) is perhaps the most screwed of all of them, having embarrassed his control freak grandma (the same pope who threatened Halandil Fang).
As a result, he's now been marched to Halandil's theatre, likely to be assassinated by his grandma in a staged killing that'll kick off a civil war between the church and the orcish people of Dol-Makjar proper.
Throughout the entire episode, absolutely nobody could roll well—a streak of terrible luck that plagued the cast during the whole thing. Absolutely terrible timing, given the walls are closing in. While earlier episodes of this campaign have had me clenching my cheeks , this one tops it.
This'd be the part of the article where I try to make predictions, but I truly, thoroughly, have no idea what's going to happen. Wicander's getting assassinated, probably by his grandmother. Tyranny's not even there, having chosen to actually go to hell (but with backup). Halandil Fang is both beloved and also marked for death. There might be a revolution and a teacher's strike going on at Murray's school.
Will the Kaedra, orcish paint angels that were created in an elaborate ritual during this very play's opening night, rush to Halandil's defense? Will the glade of fey (oh there's a glade of fey nearby, under the lake, where there is a dragon, don't worry about it) appear? Will the assassination attempt be a convincing lie—and if isn't staged, then who the hell is trying to kill Wicander?
There are so many goddamn plates spinning at this point that I haven't the faintest clue which ones are going to get knocked off their poles, but I absolutely cannot wait to see the porcelain fly.

title: Grand Theft Auto 5 is a game about shapeshifting now. I don't make the rules
text:
Los Santos Customs
I'm modding GTA 5 every day in a quest to either transform it into a PC version of GTA 6 or break it entirely. Come back tomorrow to find out what new horrible thing I've done to Rockstar's baby, or check out what I got up to earlier .
Disregard that other thing I said. Grand Theft Auto 5 no longer only launches in windowed mode. It now only launches in fullscreen mode. We're choosing not to investigate this and are just hoping the whole thing works itself out.
Another thing to disregard: what I said earlier about Hulk: Ultimate Destruction. The greatest game of all time is, in fact, 2009's Prototype, which is about being a really angry flu who can take on the appearance of anyone he eats. You can turn your arm into a sword, you fight some sort of flesh-Christ in Times Square. There's a lot going on.
Anyway GTA 5 is like Prototype now, in that I have installed Shapeshifter V . This allows you to immediately become any pedestrian you happen to stealth attack, to no real discernible end. It is quite novel, though. So an outfit you like? Take it. Also, take the in-fit. You are a great roving blob on a quest to consume and to replicate.
I am fairly certain that the act of becoming a new person doesn't change your voice, so do brace yourself for the piercing screams of Shawn Fonteno to emerge from the throats of old men and young men as they find themselves whipped up in a passing tornado or teleported a few thousand feet into the sky.
(Image credit: Rockstar) But these are bagatelles. Overall, shapeshifting is another fascinating patch in the great GTA 5 tapestry I am forging. I just have to remember to only launch that tapestry in full-screen now. Or maybe tomorrow it will be windowed again. What an adventure.

title: That's some fiiiiine lookin' milk, but Rust devs warn that 'cream is a more powerful consumable'
text:
Rust's October Update
On the heels of Facepunch Studios adding necks to s&box it has now also added milk to Rust . *️⃣
October's Rust update is here and it's bringing livestock—cows and sheep—and their various secretions, offal, and dander for all your crafting needs. The new animals produce the following:
(Image credit: Facepunch Studios) Animal stuff
Dung
Meat
Bones
Leather
Milk (cows only)
Wool (sheep only)
Companionship?
There's an economy built around these new herbivores, so in addition to murdering them for resources you can also take your animals to a new Stable vendor and haggle over the price of sale. The same vendor will also buy the wool you harvest from sheep.
New fencing has been added so you can build a pen for your pals. Here's a rundown of some of the other new livestock features:
(Image credit: Facepunch Studios) Animal stuff, cont'd
Facepunch doesn't explain how to capture livestock, but says it " should all be pretty intuitive "
Like plants, you can breed animals in search of " a god clone "
If you anger the NPC vendor by haggling too much, you'll have to wait 15 minutes before selling them something else
You can drink milk
You can refrigerate milk for four hours , and then " skim " it
Skimming milk gives you skimmed milk
Skimming milk also gives you cream
• "Cream is a more powerful consumable."
Milk and cream can be added to tea to buff its effects
Raw and spoiled meat can be used in a biofuel generator
Squirrels, rabbits, frogs, turtles, and other critters have also been added
(Image credit: Facepunch Studios) Good to finally have confirmation that cream is more powerful than milk. There's plenty of other stuff in Rust's October update but I think I covered the best of the stuff, plus it's a really long blog and I don't feel like reading the rest. Help yourself!
Footnotes
*️⃣ "On the heels of Facepunch Studios adding necks to s&box it has now also added milk to Rust" is a really weird sentence. Is it the first time that sentence has ever been said?
Oddly enough, no!
After searching for a few hours through various newspaper archives, it seem the same sentence was spoken on July 12, 1967 by Idaho governor Don Samuelson while giving a speech at the dedication of Farragut State Park. He keeled over a moment later and would remain unconscious for three days, apparently the victim of an unexplained and, quite honestly, fairly useless transmission from the future.
As he lay there on the ground twitching and mumbling, the Idaho Falls Post-Register reported, he received some "light boos" from the crowd. ⬆️

title: At last: I can build a home out of raw Windows Vista-era nostalgia
text:
Imagine for a moment: It's the year 2007. All software looks like glossy, rounded plastic, dewy glass, and photographs of verdant fields. Every electronic device makes ethereal chimes when it starts up. You've never heard the phrases 'live-service,' 'large language model,' or 'prediction market.' It's safer here, amidst the dreamy lime greens and ocean blues. It's better.
And now, thanks to a new house-builder that launched on Steam this week, we can live the definitely-healthy fantasy of retreating into the security of yesterday's software aesthetics. Frutiger Home is a home decorating sim where you can build an impregnable psychic cocoon out of the finest design elements of an era where technology could still feel optimistic, and not like perpetual cognitive radiation poisoning. Hooray!
All its architectural themes, available color swatches, and interior accent pieces are inspired by the Frutiger Aero aesthetic—a term retroactively coined by Consumer Aesthetics Research Institute co-founder Sofi Xian to describe the glossy, glassy, gleaming visual language that dominated tech and UI design from the mid-2000s to the early 2010s. Here, sharp corners are an aberration. Every surface that can be polished, will be polished.
When I loaded into an empty home to begin decorating, one wall of the living room was dominated by a screen showing clownfish and dandelions. I could change it to show a collection of citrus slices, because of course I could. Once, our devices held these images in reverence. A computer was a window to an idealized version of nature: one that was mostly seagulls and water floating through the air for some reason.
It was the Zune's time.
(Image credit: frutigerdev) After browsing the selection of furniture that looked like it was extruded straight from the dimension where sans-serif typefaces live, I stepped outside of my fully-rounded home and into a field where the impossibly green hillsides of that Windows wallpaper—you know the one—stretch into the distance, forever. You can join me here. I've placed two chairs with loops for legs. We can pretend it's 2007 for as long as we need to.
Frutiger Home is available now, on Steam , in 2026, for $5.

title: 'We needed a potentially infinite resource of party members so that we could then kill them:' Entropy dev James Wragg explains how you fit permadeath in a party RPG
text:
Entropy is a very cool, very funky RPG you can play in early access right now. It's a turn-based ode to the likes of Final Fantasy 10 or Lost Odyssey, but it's also got some PC flair—lead developer James Wragg cites Fallout 1 and Games Workshop's tabletop Mordheim as major inspirations as well. I asked Wragg about the game's mercenary hiring and ambitious permadeath system in a conversation this past summer.
In addition to the injury system, Wragg was clear that you can get through Entropy with zero casualties via skilled play. But even then, the possibility of permadeath is still there, adding an edge to the proceedings.
I felt that acutely in this year's Star Wars Zero Company, which has a similar mix of authored snowflake squadmates and procgen mercenaries. I managed to get through that game without losing anyone, but the fact that they could have died lent the story and my achievement more weight .
I've loved what I've seen of Entropy so far, but haven't gotten super far into its latest, early access build. I'm curious to see how much more story meat its authored companions will have versus the mercenaries. If Wragg and the rest of Lovely Hellplace's stance on side quests ( like em, love em, gotta have em ) is any indication, there's probably a lot to chew on there. You can check out Entropy's demo for free, and the full early access experience for $12 on Steam .

title: Kingdom Come: Deliverance studio co-founder hopes Grand Theft Auto 6 will 'blaze a trail' to higher game prices
text:
Warhorse Studios co-founder Martin Klima is just putting it out there: He isn't a fan of the Grand Theft Auto series, and has no interest in playing GTA 6 when it debuts on consoles on November 19. Nonetheless, he's hoping that it's at least as big a hit as everyone expects it to be, for one particular reason: so other studios (like his) can take advantage of the opportunity to increase their prices, a move he believes is necessary for the survival of the industry.
The Grand Theft Auto series "doesn't appeal to me at all," Klima told PC Gamer in a recent interview, and not only that, he doesn't understand why everyone else is so gaga over them either. "I am not going to be playing GTA 6 unless I'm somehow forced to," he continued. "And the reason why it is so popular—it beats me. It's something which I just fail to understand."
Klima emphasized that he bears no ill will toward the GTA games or Rockstar, and in fact he thinks "it's really good that somebody is making these games that are really technologically marvels." And he hopes that when GTA 6 finally does arrive, it lives up to the hype.
The game industry is facing a big problem, in Klima's estimation. Games are ridiculously expensive to make, a trend that is likely to continue for the foreseeable future, as computing power continues to increase and gamers accordingly expect the complexity and scale of new games to match. But the new revenue streams needed to support those endeavours just aren't there: Audience growth has been more or less maxed out, and digital marketplaces are already providing maximal returns on units sold—as Klima put it, "We destroyed retail, and we took all their money."
The last thing you can do is to increase the unit price. That would help a lot, but everybody's scared to death about it. Now, hopefully, GTA will blaze the trail, and it will allow us to increase the cost.
Martin Klima, Warhorse Studios co-founder
The Covid-19 pandemic created an "artificial demand" that goosed things for a while, but that's faded away, as evidenced by the subsequent slash-and-burn wrought by industry executives who grossly overextended themselves and are now forcing others to pay the price. So, what's left?
"The last thing you can do is to increase the unit price," Klima said. "That would help a lot, but everybody's scared to death about it. Now, hopefully, GTA will blaze the trail, and it will allow us to increase the cost."
Rockstar and Take-Two are the only ones "who can afford, or who can dare, to increase the price of games, which I think is long overdue and also necessary for this business to survive," Klima said. "So I wish them all the luck."
I find the admission refreshingly honest: Not every game executive out there is willing to admit that they really want to jack their prices but won't do it until they can put the heat for it on someone else. That's typically the sort of thing you hear from industry analysts: In May, for instance, Bank of America securities analyst Omar Dessouky called for a higher price on GTA 6 , not just for the good of Rockstar and Take-Two, but for everyone. If the next Grand Theft Auto can succeed at a higher cost, it will "raise the price point for the entire industry," he argued.
After months of speculation, Dessouky got his wish: Take-Two confirmed in June that GTA 6 will launch at $80 , $10 more than conventional big-budget games—although by locking a significant amount of content in the more expensive Ultimate Edition, it's effectively a $100 game . That's a hell of a price, but even so I suspect Klima is going to get his wish too—and once the GTA 6 price normalization has set in, we're going to see quite a few more expensive games in 2027 and beyond.

title: More than 450 Witcher 3 mods have already been updated to support the Remastered version
text:
In the mere two days since The Witcher 3: Remastered released on PC, its Nexus Mods page has been a hive of activity, featuring updates for all sorts of customization packages for the game— including ones you'll only install if you're a coward .
By my count, more than 450 Witcher 3 mods are either newly released or updated since September 29, an overwhelming number if you thought you'd just poke your head in and see what's been going on. One thing that's going on is that a lot of mods are now using AI image generation to create thumbnails that immediately give me the ick. Why create a fake, AI-glazed screenshot for your HUD mod when we all know what The Witcher 3 actually looks like? Baffling!
Another thing that's going on, thankfully, is that some modders with names like GrimReaper2121 are still putting in good work with creations such as De-mastered Geralt . And loads of mods that date back to the 2010s, making them mainstays of The Witcher 3's mod scene, have been updated to play nice with the latest patch.

title: How to conquer Kuttenberg
text:
Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2 is about a lad named Henry and his small role in kicking Sigismund of Luxembourg out of Bohemia in the name of the imprisoned King Wenceslas I. Henry and his newfound pals conspire, heist, assassinate, and sabotage to loosen the usurper's grip on the economic stronghold of Kuttenberg, but what they never try is barging straight in the front door.
Just take the damn city! It can't be that hard. I say around 20, 40 men tops could do the job. In fact, if the story quests won't do it, I will.
Step 1: Raise an army
(Image credit: Warhorse) Surprisingly, this is the easy part. KCD2, for all its freedoms, does not natively allow Henry to roam Bohemia with a warband, so the mod " Companion Squad " from Steam user Triget will be the engine powering this righteous campaign.
With just two keystrokes, my army began to take shape in front of me: 10, 20, 30 mercenaries with unique names and faces stood at attention, ready to attack at my command. The gates of Kuttenberg stood before us—doors wide open—its treasonous protectors oblivious to our plans.
Step 2: Call in favors
(Image credit: Warhorse) A "Heroes" section of the spawn menu caught my eye. With a few more clicks, I'd called up all of Henry's friends (and enemies) for a quick favor, including Hans Capon, the entire Jan Zizka crew, Godwin, Erik, Istvan Toth, and even Radzig and Hanush made the trip from Rattay.
With a strained framerate, my army was 43 strong. Time to take back Kuttenberg—for King Wenceslas!
Step 3: I have no pants
(Image credit: Warhorse, Triget on Steam) As I entered photo mode to witness the might of my army, I realized I've been pantless the whole time. This is the first time I've loaded this particular save on my newer PC, and somehow Henry's padded hose did not make the transition. They are not in my inventory and no longer seem to exist. At least I still have my mens' respect.
Step 4: Charge!
(Image credit: Warhorse, Triget on Steam) The guard who searches everyone entering the city didn't take kindly to my unsheathed sword. We exchanged a few blows before my warband formed into a bloodthirsty mob that I will henceforth call the "murder clump" and killed the guy in about two seconds. Another guard started a 1v1 with me and the murder clump ate him too.
It turned out the army was set to "defend" me, so they only raised arms when I was in an active fight. This isn't what I had in mind for a grand coup, so I pressed F6 to switch their attack pattern to something more offensive.
Step 5: Overwhelm
(Image credit: Warhorse) Finally, the murder clump branched out and started attacking guards without my direct input. Kuttenberg's finest simply did not stand a chance. With no time to prepare a proper defense and word traveling slowly throughout the town, the small squads of guards responding to the commotion were immediately overwhelmed by a blob of plate armor and sharpened steel. Once the eastern entrance was clear of law enforcement, I joined the clump and charged down the streets in the direction of city hall.
Then we passed by an inn, and I watched in horror as half of the murder clump broke off to ransack the peaceful business. This is when I realized that the army was set to "Bandit mode."
Step 6: Accidentally become the bad guys
Warhorse Warhorse Warhorse Warhorse Warhorse Warhorse The murder clump attacked everything that moved. Nobles, innkeepers, silver miners, musicians, and yes, all the guards too. Other than their tendency to get stuck in doorways, they worked with ruthless efficiency, turning a military coup into the sort of scorched-earth ransacking that upended Henry's life in the first KCD. I tried to switch between "attack" and "defend" mode to spare lives where possible, but the army had spread out into smaller murder clumps, and they didn't always listen to my commands.
This isn't how I wanted to take Kuttenberg, but it did speed the whole thing up a great deal. It took less than 20 minutes for the city to basically run out of guards, other than the ones who fled.
Step 7: Apologize to God, or something
(Image credit: Warhorse, Triget on Steam) By nightfall, the streets were bloody and quiet. I'd lost seven soldiers of my own, Hans and Zizka were super dead, and I had a foot in the grave, too, thanks to guards targeting my bare legs. We stormed city hall and found a series of empty rooms. Sigismund had presumably turned tail when he saw our numbers—the coward!
I entered a room with a little shrine and let Henry say a prayer. A quick apology for all of the senseless murder should do the trick.
Step 8: Take office
(Image credit: Warhorse, Triget on Steam) In the next room was an important-looking office with a big desk. I took my seat in a fancy chair and crowned myself king, mayor, or whatever, of Kuttenberg.
Job done, but I can't say I recommend this strategy: I have completely messed up my save by killing countless quest givers, and every town in the region wants me to hang for my crimes. But hey, it was a lot faster than finishing the main story.

title: 'Open world fatigue' is one reason indie RPG Entropy is borrowing from the classics: 'PS1, PS2, GameCube games really never outstayed their welcome'
text:
Indie RPG team Lovely Hellplace is undeniably retro-focused: 2024's Dread Delusion and the early access Entropy are crunchy and polygonal as hell. But that also extends to design. Dread Delusion was like a stripped-down Morrowind, while Entropy is a classico JRPG with some PC gaming DNA spliced in .
When I spoke to lead developer James Wragg earlier this year, he told me that he thinks part of the appeal of older games is their willingness to be succinct.
Elsewhere in our conversation, Wragg revealed that he's never beaten Breath of the Wild, and whenever he plays, he just wants to revisit 2002's Wind Waker instead. I find this issue much more acute on replays, in my own experience: I've never beaten BotW a second time after that initial playthrough where I got all the shrines (I was unemployed). More recently, I've found myself turning away from my beloved Elden Ring to the far more snackable Bloodborne and Sekiro.
Fallout is such a good shout here: I had a fairly completionist replay a few years ago, and I wrapped it in about 12 hours. Even the fact that Wragg's previous game, Dread Delusion, was open world isn't as much of a gotcha as you might think: It's a pretty dense map and boasts a roughly 15-20 hour runtime.
I find myself much more likely to stop playing a game without hitting the credits these days than to finish something and wish there had been more of it⁠—and even then, the latter is a preferable feeling in my book. There will always be a place for long runners and sprawling open worlds in my heart, but not everybody gets to be Cyberpunk 2077 or Fallout: New Vegas, and that's what makes them special.
Entropy, meanwhile, feels like it has a massive world, at least from the slice of map I've seen. But being able to evoke scale without overstaying the game's welcome is something Lovely Hellplace already managed in Dread Delusion. If you're intrigued by Entropy and Wragg's approach to design, you can check out its free demo or $12 early access on Steam .

title: One story about my first 30 minutes in this post-apocalyptic robot game led multiple people to buy it
text:
ABOVE: A brief gameplay clip from Radiosol. You can't spend too long in the sunlight.
TripletConcept TripletConcept "A journey through a desolate world burned by a planetary cataclysm"
I related this experience in PC Gamer's work chat and multiple of us bought Radiosol, called by its developers "a journey through a desolate world burned by a planetary cataclysm," on the spot. It helps that it's only $9 on Steam , and that its jaggy megastructures look exceptionally cool.
As has become habitual when I see anything that looks mildly uncanny these days, I scrolled down to the generative AI disclosure on Steam: It was used for translations, the Moscow-based developer says, but not to generate any audio or art.
On X, developer TripletConcept also states that they used AI for "some coding and utility stuff like handling Git merges." The artist has been making art in this style since before the 2020s, as evidenced by their ArtStation profile .
I'm not far into Radiosol yet, so I'm still working out what I think—this is just my first impression, not a review. But so far, it's pretty sick.
You're a little wall-climbing spider-robot in the deserted ruins of megastructures, on your way to some kind of final battle for the fate of… it's unclear. Multiple subjects are broadcasting information to you as you work your way toward a pyramid for the big fight, leaping between shadows to stay out of direct sunlight.
(Image credit: TripletConcept) So far, there's nothing in the way of combat. It's fun just being a spider-dude, executing big hops in the low-G environment—I have gotten the impression that this is not quite earth—to traverse unshaded stretches of desert. Currently, I'm seeking a "Megapol station" in the territory of the "Locus Group of Companies."
If you decided to check out Radiosol, my suggestions are A) prepare to have a lot of proper nouns thrown at you without context and B) commit the important parts of the menu layouts to memory, in the event that you can't help yourself from hitting the red button that turns off thinking.

title: If Ace Combat's too pricey, this excellent indie alternative is on sale for just $12.50
text:
If there's an Ace Combat fan in your life, you're likely already aware that it's a very good time for fighter jets dogfighting with arcade intensity. But if you're not already certain that exchanging near-infinite missiles is for you—you should be, but I acknowledge we all find truth at our own pace—Ace Combat 8's $70 price tag might seem a bit too high for a trial run.
Luckily, there's a phenomenal alternative that you can pick up for a fraction of the price: Project Wingman , a celebrated Ace Combat-inspired passion project that's currently available for $12.50 in the Steam Autumn Sale.
(Image credit: Sector D2) Project Wingman began development as a "portfolio piece" for its developers, eventually graduating to a successfully-backed Kickstarter project that nearly tripled its funding goals and ultimately launching on Steam in December 2020. It's an unabashed homage, drawing on the missile-heavy excess of its spiritual predecessors and elevating it to an even greater intensity of near-absurdist air combat.
It's more than an imitation, however: Project Wingman implemented its own roguelike Conquest Mode, where players can battle for territory against enemy squadrons and use the funds they earn in completed missions to build out their own airfleets. And unlike the latest Ace Combat—which had to issue an apology for its lackluster flight stick support—Project Wingman boasts comprehensive HOTAS compatibility for the intensive air combat sickos among us.
It's also got native VR support, if you think your stomach can tolerate the simulation of hammering a high-G turn.
(Image credit: Sector D2/Humble Games) But don't just take my word for it: Project Wingman is currently enjoying an Overwhelmingly Positive rating on Steam, where 93% of its more than 22,000 reviews are favorable. We were marginally less enthusiastic in our own Project Wingman review from 2020 due to an unsated hunger for a more hardcore flight sim experience, but if you're looking for an affordable entry into indulgent jet jousting, you'll be hard pressed to find a better option.
Project Wingman is available now on Steam at a sale price of $12.50.

title: Masters of Albion, Peter Molyneux's final game, just got a huge update and, [vigorous, lips-pursed nodding of approval], suddenly the old god game magic is back
text:
Masters of Albion 's 'New Beginnings' update launches today, and it overhauls and upgrades many of the original early access release's systems. The above video gives an overview of what's new.
I bought Masters of Albion when it launched in April. But after scoping out what's new in this update, I feel the moment that I and, no doubt, many other PC gamers have been waiting for has arrived: it's the moment when Peter Molyneux's final title has properly started to take form and genuinely recapture the god game magic of old.
Here is what's new in Masters of Albion, with commentary from Peter Molyneux on each new feature. This is followed by my personal take on the New Beginnings update.
Engine performance just doubled
(Image credit: 22cans) Nighttime gameplay is overhauled
(Image credit: 22cans) There's a brand new, card-based Arcadium
(Image credit: 22cans) Product orders now are narrative lead
(Image credit: 22cans) The design table has been reworked
(Image credit: 22cans) The Orkenstone now warps the landscape
(Image credit: 22cans) The god hand has been upgraded
(Image credit: 22cans) Masters of Albion's start has been enhanced
(Image credit: 22cans) Mysterious new colossal structures now exist
(Image credit: 22cans) My take on New Beginnings
(Image credit: 22cans) Speaking candidly, before the New Beginnings update I struggled to recommend Masters of Albion to most PC gamers. And this was because, at launch, I felt the game was lightweight, even for an early access game. It had plenty of god game systems, sure, such as building and settlement construction, product manufacturing, and combat (strategic and action), and yes, there was the famous god hand of old to wield, but much like the game's rudimentary opening, the well of what you could actually do with those systems soon ran dry.
Be that the repetitive nature of product manufacturing, the eventual grind of nighttime, or the limited way in which you could impact the world with your god hand, what you could do made you recall Molyneux's great games of old, such as Dungeon Keeper, Black & White, and Fable, but you were left wanting more, as the systems were not as complex, fleshed out, or varied.
Molyneux has since described the original release of Masters of Albion as an 'initial sketch' of a game, and in many respects that is to be expected from the very first version of an early access game, but when you're trying to combine multiple parts of other genres together for your game, individual genres that in single-genre releases tend to flesh out their core loop at the earliest moment as it is all they deliver, rather than just a facet of what they deliver, it feels a harder sell to convince gamers to get invested when your game's systems start off in a more unfinished state.
(Image credit: 22cans) To me, this ability to combine multiple genres together has always been where Molyneux has been at his creative, magical best, delivering unique experiences not offered elsewhere. But combining genres also poses its own problems, with the two most pressing being the depth of the systems and how they interact. You need the systems, such as city building and RTS combat, to be good enough to stand on their own and combine into something new, as otherwise the draw for gamers to just go play the single-genre game that does, say, RTS combat better will be too strong. Molyneux hit this problem in Black & White 2.
The good news is that the updates that New Beginnings bring all seem to directly address these two fundamental aspects in both fleshing out the bare-bones original early access release, or overhauling its core systems for the better, while adding extra interactivity and strategic weight. And I genuinely think those changes shift the game up to a whole new level. Suddenly Masters of Albion feels like a proper PC release and, while far from finished, is now in an early access state where I feel I can recommend it to god game fans, as well as PC gamers interested in getting a taste of this old-school PC gaming genre.
(Image credit: 22cans) The game's engine optimisation is also a huge deal. This was my number one criticism from playing the game at launch. Despite having a powerful gaming PC, I struggled to hit 30 fps at times, despite the game not being a AAA graphical powerhouse. A much higher fps is going to make a big difference.
Finally, what I consider to be the really tantalising addition in this update, though, is the appearance of these mysterious colossal structures that dominate the skyline—especially because they are called out in the New Beginnings press release, which asks if they are "a link to the past or a foreshadowing of the future?" This, along with Molyneux's cryptic commentary above, indicates that Masters of Albion could very well be heading towards introducing Black & White-style giant avatars in a future update. If these are added, and we continue to see this level of acting on community feedback to refine and upgrade in-game systems, maybe Masters of Albion really will evolve into the ultimate god game. And that would be a fitting swansong for the man who created the genre.

title: There's something even scarier than Huggy Wuggy in the Playtime toy factory this weekend
text:
It's been a while since I set foot nervously inside the Playtime Co. factory, but last time I was there I was hounded through the halls and air vents by a towering blue plush toy that wanted nothing more than to hug me to death.
I played a bit of the multiplayer prequel to Poppy Playtime this week, and I can now report that there's something even scarier than that giant Huggy Wuggy doll roaming the factory. Her name is Miss Delight. You can meet her yourself because the Escape from Playtime open beta is now live on Steam and you can try out the game all weekend long.
This time you're one of the cute little Playtime toys, like a plush bunny, a cartoony cat, or a fluffy unicorn, and your goal is to escape the accursed factory with your pals by skittering through the dark corridors and shadowy rooms collecting supplies. Fill a cart with enough useful junk and you can advance to the next shift. Complete all the shifts and you're free. But it's not gonna be easy.
In my session we were stalked by progressively more monstrous toys each shift we completed. There are toy robots who speed toward you when detected and explode on contact, though if a teammate bonks them in the back of the head with a thrown object first, they shut down. There's also a Cat Bee (it's a cat dressed like a bee) that latches onto players and poisons them until, again, another player knocks them off with a thrown object. You can already see the purpose of sticking together.
Then there's Miss Delight. You'll know she's around by the clicking of her high heels echoing through the factory. She, like Huggy Wuggy, is tall, towering over you (especially since you're just a little stuffed toy) and insta-murdering you if she catches you. Thing about Miss Delight is that it's simple to stop her in her tracks: just shine a flashlight in what's left of her face.
But somehow Miss Delight standing there staring at you is worse than Huggy Wuggy chasing you down. Turns out there's something worse than an unstoppable monster, and it's a monster that stops. And stands there motionless. Staring at you. With bright, shiny dead eyes a gaping, hungry mouth. Just standing there, completely still, staring… right up your flashlight battery dies.
That's not the only warning about Escape from Playtime. Mob Entertainment has one too:
"We want to emphasize that this is very much a playtest looking for your feedback," the developer says. "This build has many work-in-progress aspects, experimental features, experiments with balance, and locked away features. Your feedback from this Beta Playtest will greatly aid in the development of the launch build and beyond!"
There will be a survey after you play if you'd like to give feedback. The open beta runs until 6 pm PT on Sunday, October 4, and supports up to eight players (with at least groups of four recommended). Find the full beta details here .

title: After a record-breaking September, 'it's safe to say Steam's yearly revenue will blow past $20B for the first time'
text:
The first six months of the year were Steam's biggest , thanks to continued growth in back-catalogue sales as well as blockbuster new releases like Forza Horizon 6 and Resident Evil Requiem. As industry analysts Alinea Analytics report, September was another record breaker based on their estimated figures.
"Steam generated $1.7 billion in September 2026," Rhys Elliott, Alinea's head of market analysis, wrote, "the platform's best September to date, up 13% on the previous record, September of last year."
Wardogs was the smash hit new release of September, though Elliott noted the "hype cycles and virality" of comparably leftfield surprises Arc Raiders and Helldivers 2 were more sustained. "By this point, Helldivers 2 had made $130M (26.5% more than Wardogs) on Steam, while Arc Raiders had made about $125M (21.2% more)."
Still, Wardogs generated an estimated $86.9M on Steam in September. Elliott highlights Onimusha: Way of the Sword ($30.4M), The Blood of Dawnwalker ($26.9M), Bodycam ($24.2M), and EA Sports FC27 ($20.7M) as the other big new launches on Steam that month.
"Steam also had its best-ever Q3," Elliott wrote, "generating $5.5B (up 12% on last year). That brings the 2026 total to $16.5B so far, a 13% increase from the $14.5B Steam made in the first nine months of 2025. Given the insane release slate for the rest of the year, it's safe to say Steam's yearly revenue will blow past $20B for the first time."
He's not wrong about the rest of the year. Looking at just October's calendar shows how spoiled for choice we are.

title: I hate having to prove my brand loyalty just for the chance to buy hardware at full price
text:
Nobody likes scalpers, man—it's already hard enough to get the latest and greatest hardware, let alone with some enterprising bad actor and their bots buying up all the available stock, and then charging an even greater fortune for sought-after bits of kit. That said, I'm not really a big fan of the anti-scalper measures many vendors are now deploying either.
For instance, Sony Japan has rolled out an anti-scalper lottery system for PS5 Pro orders. To be in with even a chance of picking up the pricey console , you'll need a Sony account registered in Japan that has logged at least 60 hours or more of gaming , either on a PS4, a PS5, or both (via Tom's Hardware ). In theory, that should be enough of a faff to deter scalpers and an easy enough hurdle for PlayStation fans to overcome. In practice, I'm not loving the weird precedent of locking my potential hardware purchases behind a dystopian brand loyalty test.
Obviously, it's not just Sony that's up to such silliness. Most recently, Valve implemented a reservation system for the launch of the Steam Frame . To sign up, the FAQ says, "You must have a Steam account in good standing," and that "You must have made a purchase on Steam prior to April 27th 2026."
To be fair to Valve, I did see reports of the Steam Machine being scalped for over $3,000 . But 'In good standing'? What does that even mean ? I couldn't find a precise definition from Valve itself; an account 'in good standing' could mean one not subject to a ban or any community restrictions, or it could mean an account that has made a purchase within a recent timeframe, or it could mean whatever suits Valve at any given moment. I'm still a little unclear on this finer point.
I've already written about how it's been genuinely cheaper for me to fly internationally to either QuakeCon or PAX West earlier this year , and pick up an RTX 5090 for MSRP at either of those in-person events. The latter scheme was described as 'Verified Priority Access IRL'. For those who don't recall, VPA was the draw system Nvidia used to offer the chance to pay full price for RTX 5090 or RTX 5080 Founders Edition graphics cards last year ( Newegg's Shuffle lottery system also did a similar thing).
「PlayStation®5 Pro」のソニーストアでの購入申し込みを、本日9月28日（月）より受け付けます。ご応募・ご購入には条件がございます。ご応募数が販売予定台数を超えた場合は抽選となりますので、あらかじめご了承ください。詳しくはこちら⇒ https://t.co/h4rOIltI9Q https://t.co/71VaLlu5ed September 28, 2026
Zotac even attempted to beat those dastardly GPU scalpers by selling RTX 50-series graphics cards to actual gamers via Discord last year. And like Nvidia, Zotac likely knew it could sell every card it offered up through such a direct (not to mention exclusive) channel.
I hate this trend, even if it is all meant to deter scalpers. I firmly believe gaming, and PC gaming especially, should be for everyone, though I'll acknowledge it rarely lives up to that ideal. Brand loyalty tests like this, plus the runaway pricing caused by the ongoing memory supply crisis, mean those without deep reserves of both cash and time are still stuck on the outside looking in. Bottom line, though scalpers may be mostly closed out of the loop by reservation systems with set qualifying criteria, I'm not convinced this is the best deal for hardware consumers.

title: Turns out you can download more battery as Valve's latest update for Steam Frame adds up to 12%
text:
Valve has pushed yet another update for SteamOS on the Steam Frame . It includes power efficiency improvements, eye tracking accessibility, and improved streaming reliability. Also something about grabbing handles?
Improved power efficiency and battery lifetime during both streaming and local gameplay, with gains of up to 12%. Note: Result vary depending on framerate and content.
Added accessibility option for users who want to limit eye tracking to a single eye. VR Settings -> General -> Track Dominant Eye Only. (requires enabling "show advanced settings")
Fixed an issue that prevented controller bindings from loading for certain games, including Google Earth VR and Thumper.
Improved focus behavior when interacting with grab/resize handles
Further VR streaming reliability improvements, including additional fixes for “Error 17.” Note: On the PC, you must also opt into SteamVR 2.18.2 or later to reduce “Error 17” connection issues. At the time of this release, SteamVR 2.18.2 is available on the SteamVR [beta] branch.
Fixed steam frame wireless adapter connectivity issues that affected users in some countries.
It's the battery life improvements that most will feel the benefit of. A 12% improvement is pretty impressive for a single software update—the Steam Frame runs for around two hours while streaming , so you're looking at another 15 minutes or so from that bump alone. Though, as Valve notes, that's dependent on what you're playing and the power setting.
Valve also recently improved charging on the Steam Frame, allowing it to fast charge even when the headset is turned off. That dramatically decreases charging times in my testing .
SteamOS for Steam Frame is a whole new project for Valve. A version of its Arch-based Linux distro, used on the Steam Machine and Steam Deck , except built for virtual reality and Arm-based processors. Specifically, the Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 in the Frame, though laying the foundations for any further Arm-powered projects. I'd love to see an Arm-powered Steam Deck, though a recent rumour suggests the Steam Deck 2 will use another AMD chip instead .

title: Unscrupulous Airbnb host tries to get $1,700 out of Redditor with AI-generated pic of overflowing toilet
text:
Photo of a toilet airbnb sent in justification for leaving damages. they are demanding 1700$ over this. It feels inconsistent with AI qualities like the water dripping from the toilet but no splashes. the entire house should flood at this point. and the door handle is at eye level  from  r/isthisAI There are few things that give me the heebie-jeebies more than overflowing toilets, burst pipes, and water damage. Ditto receiving a hefty, unexpected fee. So I wonder, how would it feel to be on the receiving end of both?
One Redditor can answer this question , though only thanks to the smoke and mirrors economy of digital manipulation. Apparently, they found themselves on the wrong end of an Airbnb host—"one of the biggest Airbnb companies of their state in Australia"—who attempted to get them to cough up $1,700 for an overflowed toilet, the evidence for which was, you guessed it, AI-generated.
So thanks, AI, in addition to making our precious PC memory very expensive , you've also made it very easy for people to attempt to fleece others using the humble commode.
Thankfully, it's AI that can also come to the rescue here, as Gemini is able to spot its own SynthID watermark in the fake image. Not that it wasn't suspected in the first place, given the Reddit post was shared on r/isthisAI .
This story has a happy ending, anyway:
"Good news everyone! I had this case resolved and deemed ineligible for the reimbursement they asked for... Also another detail I forgot to mention is that there is a floor underneath this one so if there are a few inches of water on the ground the entire first floor should be an aquarium!"
Regardless of how things went in this particular case, I'm using this as a reminder for myself: take pictures and record videos of any Airbnbs you stop at just before you leave. Better to be safe than sorry.

title: Looks like you will have to pinky promise you won't export your RTX 5090 if you buy a gaming PC from Micro Center now
text:
Form for 5090’s  from  r/Microcenter With price gouging and some buyers exporting graphics cards to China, Micro Center is reportedly making customers swear they won't do the same. And with a signed declaration, it's maybe a bit more airtight than a pinky promise.
This is according to Reddit user Krothic , who recently picked up a Powerspec Ai90 prebuilt PC with an RTX 5090 in it and was hit with the form. The Redditor bought the PC from a Micro Center in Tustin, California, and according to the manager, the new anti-export declaration only came into effect a few days ago.
High-end GPUs have been banned from being exported to China as America is looking to win the AI race, and more beefy cards in the country equals more power. But it's also become harder to actually buy an RTX 5090 GPU on its own, with the likes of Newegg and Amazon's only listings being shops with questionable provenance and names such as 'sdflkjahsdgasdggbsd'. Full PCs, then, might be your only recourse for grabbing a card for export if that is your aim.
Apparently, the user had to hand over their driver's license to verify their identity, too, linking their purchase to their name. Should that GPU be found being shipped elsewhere, Micro Center could technically tie the GPU back to the buyer by checking its serial number. But this doesn't account for someone buying a prebuilt, then deciding to one day sell that on or eventually giving it to someone else.
In fairness, the paper does get the buyer to state, "I am purchasing this product for my own legitimate personal or business use in the United States, or I have accurately identified the actual end user above." But that still feels like a lot of paperwork just to buy a new PC, and that's before we get into how enforceable any of this is.
(Image credit: Future) If an exported GPU is tied back to someone who purchased one at Micro Center, there are reasons one could claim for how the GPU ended up there, ie, it being stolen.
It seems likely the biggest deterrent to exporting is not the declaration but, in fact, the ID check. If you are looking to export cards en masse, you likely won't want to give your full legal name to an entity that can tie those purchases back to you.
Still, it's getting harder and harder to buy gaming hardware, and not just because of the price. The barriers to entry are being raised, and many brands are opting to have users prove brand loyalty to get the tech instead . Neither option seems that appealing to me.

title: Riot needed absurd player counts 'in the high hundreds of thousands, if not millions' for 2XKO, dooming it from launch
text:
2XKO ending its development (which Merrill phrases here as turning it into a "box game" instead, despite the fact Riot also laid off a bunch of people to make that happen), came as a deep frustration, but not much of a surprise given the current nightmare year the industry's been having. However—that number, "high hundreds of thousands, if not millions", is a somewhat desperate number.
Especially given the podcast has an annotation of monthly active users (MAU), which one'd assume would mean they asked Merrill for clarification. An active user is a unique user that logs in and does something at least once during a month, which means that the number would be far higher than concurrent users (how many of those users are logged in at any one time).
However, we can at least make some very loose guesstimates. Street Fighter 6 has a 30,000 concurrent peak on PC at the time of writing. Let's assume the average person has a seven hour window during a day to play, accounting for a nine to five job or chores/social obligations on the weekend—the concurrent count doesn't actually jump that much.
So let's say that in a 24 hour period, you've got around 30-35% of your potential playerbase online at any given moment. The rest are sleeping, working, running errands, etc. That leaves SF6 with roughly 100,000 people who are consistently playing the game on PC every day.
I wanna note: This is by no means an accurate number, it's kitchen napkin math and guesswork that assumes there's an even amount of SF6 players in each time zone and that they each have the same daily schedule but look, I'm working with what I have here (Capcom doesn't have monthly active users info available).
Let's be extremely generous and say only 25% play on PC, something that likely isn't even the case , I'm steelmanning myself here—that still leaves us with 400,000 players total in a 24-hour period. Monthly active users, though, is simply a tallying of: "Did this person log in at any point during the month". Assuming no new players came to SF6, that 400,000 daily total player count wouldn't change its impact on the MAU number.
Which means that you'd have to be getting in a lot of new or returning players every single day to bump up the monthly unique player count to anywhere near one million. SF6 has sold 7 million units total between June 2023 and June 2026. Even if you spread that out over the 36 months between those two dates (unlikely, sales are usually frontloaded) that'd still be just 194,444 potential additions to the pool every month.
In other words, even if you take one of the most popular fighting games in the world, with the most generous read possible on its total daily active user count, with the most disadvantageous PC/Console split to make my point, you'd still barely get over the 500,000 monthly active user mark. Shy of "high hundreds of thousands", and certainly shy of "millions" plural.
The comparison becomes weirder when you compare it to other fighting games that are still receiving support. Guilty Gear: Strive is still getting new characters and updates, and that has a 24-hour concurrent peak of 1,580.
In other words: There was no way in hell that 2XKO was ever going to get enough in the way of players to satisfy its expectations, which leaves a lot of questions here. Did Riot as a company just get overconfident from less niche genres? Did it not do the market research? Were the 2XKO developers just super inefficient?
Or did it simply have enough money to, like many studios before it, simply gamble and see if it could create something even better than Street Fighter 6—rolling the dice on the livelihoods of the developers who were making it? None of the answers to those questions are particularly flattering.
